# Core declarations: actions, records, regions, state

Canonical: https://plingjs.dev/reference/core-declarations-actions-records-regions-state

Pling exposes a page to a model through four kinds of declarations. They answer different questions and are deliberately not interchangeable:

| Declaration | Question it answers | Write path |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Action | What can be done here? | Yes |
| Record | Which object is this, and what does it contain? | No |
| Region | Where is this, and is it currently reachable? | No |
| State | What view is currently in effect? | No |

Only actions write. Records, regions, and state describe; they never become a second execution channel.

## Actions

An action is a stable id, a description written for the model, a risk kind, and an execution route. The route is either a DOM primitive (`click`, `fill`, `select`, `press`, `hover`), an injected `run`, or a `handoff` that asks the user to complete the step.

| Field | Required | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | Recommended | Generated once for element bindings | Stable ids are mandatory for list rows and task continuity |
| `desc` | Yes | — | The model's only explanation of the operation |
| `kind` | No | `"write"` | `"read"`, `"write"`, or `"danger"` |
| `params` | No | — | Array shorthand or JSON Schema; array params are required unless `optional: true` |
| `run` | No | DOM primitive | Receives validated, unmasked arguments |
| `available` | No | — | `false` or a string makes the action unavailable; the string is shown to the model |
| `expect` | No | — | Waits for a result; failure becomes `EXPECTATION_FAILED` |
| `confirm` | No | Derived from the policy | `true` or `"always"` |
| `handoff` | No | — | The user completes the step; `run` is not executed |
| `action` / `target` / `autoTarget` / `fidelity` | No | Inferred | Control how a DOM primitive resolves its target |

```ts [Vue 3]
const submit = { id: "add_task", desc: "Add a task from the composer", kind: "write" };
```

```tsx [React]
const submit = usePlingTool<HTMLButtonElement>({
  id: "add_task",
  desc: "Add a task from the composer",
  kind: "write",
});
```

```ts [Vanilla / jQuery]
const off = pling.tool(document.querySelector("#add")!, {
  id: "add_task",
  desc: "Add a task from the composer",
  kind: "write",
});
```

```ts [Vue 2.7]
// <button v-tool="{ id: 'add_task', desc: 'Add a task from the composer' }">
// The directive accepts the same ToolOptions shape.
```

Declaring an action does not guarantee it is visible. Disabled elements, covered elements, inactive regions, and failed `available()` checks remove it from the model's action list and attach a reason. This is intentional: “not registered” and “temporarily unavailable” are different states and should remain distinguishable.

## Records

A record gives a row an identity and a bounded set of fields. The identity must come from the business object, not from its position in the array.

```ts [Vue 3]
// <li v-for="task in tasks" :key="task.id" v-record="{ data: task, label: task.title }">
```

```tsx [React]
const row = usePlingRecord({ data: task, label: task.title });
return <li ref={row}>{task.title}</li>;
```

```ts [Vanilla / jQuery]
const off = pling.record(rowElement, { data: task, label: task.title });
```

```ts [Vue 2.7]
// <li v-for="task in tasks" :key="task.id" v-record="{ data: task, label: task.title }">
```

Defaults:

- id: `data.id`, then `data.key`;
- fields: the data object without the id field;
- scope: the nearest enclosing region;
- order: page order when the adapter can determine it.

Records are read-only. A row action is still an action and still goes through availability, policy, execution, and expectation checks. Do not try to encode “mark complete” as a record field change.

## Regions

A region gives the page a small structure tree. It also participates in visibility and reachability.

| Field | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | Yes | Stable, language-independent |
| `label` | No | Human-readable name shown to the model |
| `description` | No | What the region is for |
| `role` | No | `main`, `dialog`, `toolbar`, `list`, and the other `RegionRole` values |
| `parent` | No | Explicit parent when DOM ancestry is not the right tree |

```ts [Vue 3]
// <section v-scope="{ id: 'todo_list', label: 'Task list', role: 'list' }">
```

```tsx [React]
const listScope = usePlingScope<HTMLUListElement>({
  id: "todo_list",
  label: "Task list",
  role: "list",
});
return <ul ref={listScope}>…</ul>;
```

```ts [Vanilla / jQuery]
const off = pling.scope(listElement, { id: "todo_list", label: "Task list", role: "list" });
```

```ts [Vue 2.7]
// <ul v-scope="{ id: 'todo_list', label: 'Task list', role: 'list' }">
```

A region is not a permission boundary. It reduces and explains what the model can reach at this moment. Authorization still belongs to the action implementation or the server.

## State

A state view is a named, read-only object that explains the current projection: active filter, applied search, counts, pagination, or the selected tab. It has no setter.

```ts [Vue 3]
useAgentState("task_view", () => ({
  filter: filter.value,
  search: appliedSearch.value,
  matched: visibleTasks.value.length,
  total: tasks.value.length,
}), { description: "Current filter, applied search, and task counts" });
```

```tsx [React]
usePlingState("task_view", () => ({
  filter,
  search: appliedSearch,
  matched: visibleTasks.length,
  total: tasks.length,
}), { description: "Current filter, applied search, and task counts" });
```

```ts [Vanilla / jQuery]
const off = pling.state("task_view", () => ({
  filter,
  search: appliedSearch,
  matched: visibleTasks.length,
  total: tasks.length,
}), { description: "Current filter, applied search, and task counts" });
```

```ts [Vue 2.7]
useAgentState("task_view", () => ({
  filter: this.filter,
  search: this.appliedSearch,
  matched: this.visibleTasks.length,
  total: this.tasks.length,
}));
```

The reader runs for every snapshot. A plain object is evaluated once at registration and will freeze the initial values. Expose the view the user is seeing, not the whole store.

## How the four declarations compose

A reliable page usually needs all four in the same region:

- the region identifies the list and controls whether it is reachable;
- records identify the rows and provide the data needed to choose one;
- actions describe the operations available on the list or a row;
- state explains filters and counts that are not visible from the rows alone.

This is the difference between “the model can click a button” and “the model can understand the current screen before choosing an action”.

## Failure modes

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The model invents an action id | The action was never registered, or its id changes between renders | Declare it explicitly and use a stable id |
| A row action targets the wrong row | The id came from the array index | Use the business key |
| A count is correct once and then stale | A plain object captured setup-time values | Read through a function |
| A dialog action remains available behind the overlay | The dialog has no region, or the overlay is not detectable | Put the dialog in a `dialog` region and verify hit testing |
| The model tries to write through state | The corresponding action is missing or poorly described | Add the action the user would use; keep state read-only |
| Two rows share an action id | The id lacks the row key | Use `toggle@${task.id}` or a namespaced id |

## Version and compatibility

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Applies to | `@plingjs/core` `0.1.0-alpha.2` |
| Introduced | `0.1.0-alpha.2` (first published alpha) |
| Runtime | Browsers with ES2022 modules; Node.js 20 or later for Node-side use |
| Peer dependencies | None |
| Stability | Pre-1.0 alpha; a minor release may change the API |

All four declarations are present in each adapter at this version. The adapter table below is the compatibility boundary; a change to a declaration's meaning would be a breaking change, not a documentation adjustment.

| Adapter | Actions | Records | Regions | State |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Vue 3 | Supported | Supported | Supported | Supported |
| React | Supported | Supported | Supported | Supported |
| Vanilla / jQuery | Supported | Supported | Supported | Supported |
| Vue 2.7 | Supported | Supported | Supported | Supported |

The status differs by adapter. The support tables in the [Vue 3 adapter](/reference/vue-3-adapter), [React adapter](/reference/react-adapter), [Vanilla / jQuery adapter](/reference/vanilla-jquery-adapter), and [Vue 2.7 adapter](/reference/vue-2-adapter) references define the exact boundary for each framework. Vue 2.7 is a real adapter, but only for the subset listed on its page.

- [Table rows and batch actions](/recipes/table-rows-and-batch-actions) applies records and row actions to a table.

# Agent runtime, sessions, context, limits

Canonical: https://plingjs.dev/reference/agent-runtime-sessions-context-limits

Page declarations describe a surface. The agent runtime decides how a conversation uses that surface: which model it calls, how much history it keeps, when an action needs approval, and what evidence remains after a run.

This page separates terms that are often used interchangeably. A configuration mistake in one layer should not be diagnosed as a problem in another.

## The objects and what they count

| Object | What it represents | Important boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `AgentRuntime` | One wired conversation environment: model client, policy, hooks, telemetry, session | Configuration is resolved once per mounted runtime |
| `AgentSession` | The dialogue goal, history, event stream, pending approvals, and pending handoffs | `send()` is serialized; a second send waits for the first |
| Turn | One model response and its tool calls inside a single `send()` | Bounded by `limits.maxTurns` |
| Model call | One request to the model provider, including retries | Counted by telemetry; may exceed the turn count |
| Context used for compaction | Base system prompt, compressed summary, and recent messages | Bounded by `limits.contextTokens`, not by the response length |

`maxTurns` is not a request limit. If the model performs five tool rounds and then answers, that is six turns. If a provider retries once after a network failure, the turn count does not change, but the model-call count does.

`maxTokens` is also a different setting. It is the provider's output limit for one response. `contextTokens` is the history budget used to decide when to compact. The per-turn page snapshot, tool schemas, and rebuilt system prompt are added after that decision, so the final provider request can exceed the nominal history budget.

## Configuration and precedence

The runtime resolves configuration in this order:

1. framework defaults;
2. environment values such as `VITE_AGENT_BASE_URL` and `VITE_AGENT_MODEL`;
3. explicit values passed through `createPling({ agent: { config } })`, a surface's `config` prop, or an injected model.

Explicit values win per field. Nested `limits` and `retry` values are merged instead of replacing the entire object.

| Field | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `baseUrl` | empty | OpenAI-compatible endpoint; a relative path uses the same-origin proxy |
| `model` | empty | Provider model identifier |
| `apiKey` | empty | Bearer token for a direct request |
| `temperature` | `0.3` | Generation randomness |
| `maxTokens` | `1024` | Output limit for one response |
| `systemPrompt` | empty | Application role appended to the framework rules |
| `stream` | `true` | Consume server-sent text deltas when supported |
| `defaultApproval` | `"danger"` | Default action policy when an action omits `confirm` |
| `minActionIntervalMs` | `0` | Minimum delay between actions in the same batch |
| `retry.maxRetries` | `3` | Retries after the first failed request; range 0 to 5 |
| `retry.baseDelayMs` | `500` | Initial exponential-backoff delay |
| `retry.maxDelayMs` | `4000` | Delay ceiling |
| `limits.maxTurns` | `10` | Model turns allowed inside one `send()` |
| `limits.contextTokens` | `8192` | History budget used for compaction; page context and tool schemas are additional |
| `limits.reserveForOutput` | `1024` | Context reserved for the next response |
| `limits.compactRatio` | `0.8` | Fraction of usable context that triggers compaction |
| `limits.keepRecent` | `6` | Recent messages kept verbatim during compaction |

An injected `llm` is sufficient for a deterministic test or a custom gateway client. In that case `baseUrl` and `apiKey` are not required for readiness. The runtime still checks limits and retry values.

## What compaction does

The history budget is not the same as the provider's full context window. Pling reserves space for the next response and compacts early:

```text
usable = contextTokens - reserveForOutput
compactAt = floor(usable × compactRatio)
```

With the defaults, `8192 - 1024 = 7168` tokens are usable and compaction starts at about `5734` tokens.

When the estimated history exceeds that line, the runtime summarizes older messages and keeps the latest `keepRecent` messages. It must not split an assistant tool-call message from its tool result; doing so produces an invalid message sequence. The system prompt is rebuilt for each request, so the model always sees the current page instead of a cached page snapshot.

Compaction preserves the task goal, decisions, constraints, and unfinished work. It is not a transcript archive. If the application needs an auditable conversation log, record session events outside the context window.

## Wiring the runtime

The same `agent` options reach the shared runtime in every adapter. Only the mount code differs.

```ts [Vue 3]
import { createPling } from "@plingjs/vue";

const pling = createPling({
  agent: {
    config: {
      limits: { maxTurns: 100, contextTokens: 16_384, keepRecent: 8 },
      retry: { maxRetries: 2 },
    },
    onEvent(event) {
      if (event.type === "error") console.warn(event.code, event.message);
    },
  },
});
```

```tsx [React]
import { createPling, PlingProvider, AgentDock } from "@plingjs/react";

const pling = createPling({
  agent: {
    config: { limits: { maxTurns: 100, contextTokens: 16_384, keepRecent: 8 } },
  },
});

export function App() {
  return (
    <PlingProvider pling={pling}>
      <TodoPage />
      <AgentDock />
    </PlingProvider>
  );
}
```

```ts [Vanilla / jQuery]
import { createPling } from "@plingjs/vanilla";

const pling = createPling({
  agent: {
    config: { limits: { maxTurns: 100, contextTokens: 16_384, keepRecent: 8 } },
    onEvent(event) {
      if (event.type === "error") console.warn(event.code, event.message);
    },
  },
});

pling.dock({ title: "Order assistant" });
```

```ts [Vue 2.7]
import Vue from "vue";
import { createPling } from "@plingjs/vue2";

const pling = createPling({
  agent: {
    config: { limits: { maxTurns: 100, contextTokens: 16_384, keepRecent: 8 } },
  },
});

Vue.use(pling.plugin);
pling.dock({ title: "Order assistant" });
```

`maxTurns: 100` is appropriate for a long tutorial or demo. Production defaults to 10. Raising the limit increases the possible cost of one user request and should be paired with a per-run or per-tenant budget.

## Tool lifecycle hooks

Tool hooks are an application-level policy seam, not another declaration mechanism. `PreToolUse` runs after the model has chosen an action but before the executor reaches the business control. It may block the call. A blocked call returns `HOOK_BLOCKED`, emits a `blocked` event, and does not run the business handler. `PostToolUse` runs after execution and may return a replacement result; later hooks and the final tool message see the replacement.

| Hook | Runs | May change | Still cannot |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `PreToolUse` | After action selection, before execution | Block with a reason; inspect the action id, model tool name, arguments, and turn | Create an undeclared action, approve itself, or bypass the executor |
| `PostToolUse` | After execution | Replace the structured result returned to the model and event stream | Undo a business side effect or turn a failed result into an executed action |

```ts
import { HookRegistry } from "@plingjs/agent";
import { createPling } from "@plingjs/vue";

const hooks = new HookRegistry();

const removePre = hooks.addPreToolUse(({ id }) => {
  if (id.startsWith("delete")) {
    return { blocked: true, reason: "Deletion requires a separate approval policy" };
  }
});

const removePost = hooks.addPostToolUse(({ result }) => {
  if ("error" in result) return;
  return { result: { ...(result.result as Record<string, unknown>), email: "[redacted]" } };
});

const pling = createPling({
  agent: { config: { limits: { maxTurns: 100 } }, hooks },
});

// Call these when the owning plugin or policy module unloads.
removePre();
removePost();
```

Hooks run in registration order. A pre-hook stops the chain on the first block; a post-hook's non-`undefined` return becomes the input to the next hook. Keep both handlers deterministic and bounded. Do not use a post-hook as the only redaction boundary for page observations: `sensitive()` governs declared outbound values, while hooks operate on action results. Do not log raw arguments or results by default; they may contain business or personal data.

Because hooks sit in the runtime rather than in the page adapter, all four adapters share the same behaviour. They are suitable for tenant policy, a kill switch for one capability, result masking, metrics, or a review queue. They are not a durable audit log and they do not decide backend authorization.

## Session lifecycle

`AgentSession` exposes:

| Method or property | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `send(input)` | Adds the user message and runs the loop; concurrent calls are serialized |
| `cancel()` | Aborts the in-flight model request and stops at the next safe point |
| `reset()` | Clears messages, summary, continuity state, and current-run counters; approval and handoff queues must be cleared separately |
| `status()` | Reports `idle`, `running`, or `cancelled`; approval and handoff waits are exposed through their queues and events |
| `events()` | Returns the UI event stream used by the chat and activity views; the session itself does not enforce a length limit |
| `continuity` | Reports whether a cross-document checkpoint is active |

Clearing the visible transcript without calling `reset()` is not a new conversation. The old history may still be sent on the next request. The built-in clear control calls `session.reset()` and also clears the approval and handoff queues and resets telemetry. A host that calls `reset()` directly must perform those queue and telemetry steps itself.

## Observability

Three records answer different questions:

- session events describe what the user and interface saw: messages, actions, approvals, handoffs, errors;
- telemetry summarizes model calls, tool calls, tokens, estimated cost, duration, retries, and error rate;
- a trace stores the exact recent model requests, including messages and tool schemas, for debugging.

Traces are opt-in and bounded. They are diagnostic data, not an audit log, and they may contain page text or prompt content. Do not retain them by default in production.

| Adapter | Runtime diagnostics |
| --- | --- |
| Vue 3 | `<AgentDock :debug="{ maxCalls: 8 }">` includes the request trace in the activity view |
| React | `AgentDock.onSessionEvent`, `createPling({ agent: { onEvent } })`, and injected telemetry; no built-in inspector |
| Vanilla / jQuery | `onSessionEvent`, then render the events in the host application |
| Vue 2.7 | Shared vanilla dock events; no built-in inspector |

## Failure modes

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `NOT_CONFIGURED` before any request | `baseUrl`, `model`, or a direct endpoint's `apiKey` is missing | Fill `.env.local` or pass an explicit `config` |
| A run stops after a few turns without a final answer | `maxTurns` was reached; this ends with a notice rather than a structured error | Inspect the session events, then raise the limit deliberately |
| The answer forgets an earlier decision | Compaction replaced old messages with a summary | Reduce tool output, expose a smaller state view, or keep the relevant decision in application state |
| A long run becomes unexpectedly expensive | `maxTurns` or `maxTokens` is high, or retries are multiplying calls | Set budgets and inspect telemetry by request |
| Context never compacts | Estimated tokens stay below the threshold or the input is still small | Do not force compaction; inspect the actual context size |
| A reset does not hide old history | The UI was cleared without `session.reset()` | Reset the session and the queues together |
| A provider sends no streaming text | `stream` is enabled but the gateway does not support SSE | Disable streaming or fix the gateway |

## Evidence

- Runtime and limit defaults: `packages/agent/src/config.ts`.
- Context compaction: `packages/agent/src/history.ts`.
- Session behavior: `packages/agent/src/session.ts`.
- Bounded debug trace in Vue 3: `examples/recipes/vue3`.
- Model settings: `packages/vue/src/model-settings.ts`.

## Version and compatibility

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Applies to | `@plingjs/agent` `0.1.0-alpha.2` |
| Introduced | `0.1.0-alpha.2` (first published alpha) |
| Runtime | Browsers with ES2022 modules; Node.js 20 or later for Node-side use |
| Peer dependencies | None |
| Stability | Pre-1.0 alpha; a minor release may change the API |

The limits and defaults on this page come from `packages/agent/src/config.ts` at this version. Session, context, compaction, and limit fields are pre-1.0; after a minor upgrade, re-read this page instead of assuming the earlier defaults still apply.

# UI messages, theme, locale

Canonical: https://plingjs.dev/reference/ui-messages-theme-locale

Pling's built-in assistant has one UI controller across Vue 3, React, Vanilla / jQuery, and Vue 2.7. It owns the framework's own labels, theme tokens, and language selection. It does not own the application's business copy.

This distinction matters. Translating a checkout button belongs to the application's i18n system. Translating “Approve”, “Clear conversation”, or “Waiting for your confirmation” in the built-in surface belongs to Pling.

## Defaults and resolution

The default locale is `en-US`. The framework does not silently follow the browser language. Browser detection is opt-in with `locale: "auto"`.

| `ui.locale` value | Result |
| --- | --- |
| omitted | `en-US` |
| `"en-US"`, `"en-GB"`, `"zh-CN"`, `"zh-TW"` | exact or base-language match in the built-in catalog |
| unsupported locale | English fallback |
| `"auto"` | first matching browser language, then English |

Locale matching is case-insensitive and treats `_` and `-` alike. A missing translation key first falls back to English, then to the key itself. Do not rely on the key as production copy.

## Options

```ts
createPling({
  ui: {
    locale: "en-US",
    theme: {
      mode: "auto",
      tokens: {
        colorPrimary: "#0f766e",
        colorPrimaryStrong: "#115e59",
        radiusLg: "16px",
      },
    },
    messages: {
      "zh-CN": {
        "chat.empty": "可以问我当前页面上的任务。",
      },
    },
    classNames: {
      dock: "product-dock",
      panel: "product-panel",
      launcher: "product-launcher",
      chat: "product-chat",
    },
  },
});
```

| Option | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `locale` | Built-in UI language; defaults to English |
| `theme` | `light`, `dark`, `auto`, or `{ mode, tokens }` |
| `messages` | Per-locale overrides for framework message keys |
| `classNames` | Four application-owned hooks: `dock`, `panel`, `launcher`, `chat` |

Theme tokens become CSS variables on the mounted surface, for example `--pling-color-primary`, `--pling-color-surface`, and `--pling-radius-lg`. Application CSS can use those variables without reaching into component internals.

`classNames` is not a second theme system. It exists for layout and brand selectors that cannot be expressed by color, radius, shadow, or typography tokens.

## Changing language and theme at runtime

```ts
pling.ui.setLocale("zh-CN");
pling.ui.setTheme({ mode: "dark" });
pling.ui.setTheme("auto");
```

The controller notifies mounted surfaces in place. React reads it through `useSyncExternalStore`; Vue and the vanilla dock subscribe to the same snapshot. A locale change does not recreate the agent session or lose its history.

The current implementation adds an explicit response-language instruction only for Chinese locales (`zh*`). Other locales rely on the base rule: answer in the language of the user's latest message. Switching the UI to English therefore does not force English answers. The UI locale is a default for explanations, not a restriction on the user.

## Adapter wiring

### Vue 3

```ts
const pling = createPling({
  ui: { locale: "en-US", theme: { mode: "auto" } },
});

pling.ui.setLocale("zh-CN");
```

### React

```tsx
const pling = createPling({
  ui: { locale: "en-US", theme: { mode: "auto" } },
});

export function App() {
  return (
    <PlingProvider pling={pling}>
      <TodoPage />
      <AgentDock />
    </PlingProvider>
  );
}
```

Use `usePlingUi()` when application controls need the current snapshot:

```tsx
const ui = usePlingUi();
ui.locale;
ui.resolvedTheme;
ui.cssVars;
```

### Vanilla / jQuery

```ts
const pling = createPling({
  ui: { locale: "en-US", theme: { mode: "auto" } },
});

pling.dock();
pling.ui.subscribe(() => {
  document.documentElement.dataset.plingTheme = pling.ui.resolvedTheme;
});
```

### Vue 2.7

```ts
import Vue from "vue";
import { createPling } from "@plingjs/vue2";

const pling = createPling({
  ui: { locale: "en-US", theme: { mode: "auto" } },
});

Vue.use(pling.plugin);
pling.dock();
```

The Vue 2.7 adapter uses the shared vanilla dock, so it exposes the same `ui` controller and language catalog. It does not have Vue 3's component slots or the Vue 3-only model-settings and debug panels.

## Language boundaries

| Text | Owner | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| “Approve”, “Cancel”, “Waiting for your confirmation” | Pling catalog | Part of the built-in interaction |
| “Save order”, “Customer since 2021” | Application | Business meaning and brand voice |
| Error codes and their short explanations | Pling catalog | Stable across adapters |
| Server error details | Application or gateway | May contain domain-specific recovery instructions |
| Model answer | Model, guided by UI locale and the latest user message | The user may switch languages at any turn |

Do not send the whole application translation catalog into the model context. The UI controller only needs the keys used by the built-in surface.

`agent.config.systemPrompt` is appended after the framework rules. It can add application context, but it cannot replace the base rule that follows the user's latest message.

## Failure modes

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Browser is Chinese but the assistant opens in English | Default is English; browser detection is opt-in | Pass `locale: "auto"` or let the user choose |
| A custom locale shows English text | The key is missing from the custom catalog | Add the key or accept the documented English fallback |
| Theme changes but the page does not | The application controls read `pling.ui.theme` instead of `resolvedTheme` | Use `resolvedTheme` for rendered colors |
| A locale switch clears the conversation | The host recreated the whole Pling instance | Call `pling.ui.setLocale()` instead |
| Custom class has no effect | It is a `classNames` slot, not an arbitrary component prop | Use `dock`, `panel`, `launcher`, or `chat` |
| Model answers in a language different from the UI | For non-Chinese locales, no extra response-language instruction is added; the latest user message still governs | Ask the user to switch languages explicitly, or add an application-level instruction that does not contradict the latest message |

## Evidence

- Shared UI controller: `packages/ui/src/controller.ts`.
- Theme token resolution: `packages/ui/src/theme.ts`.
- Locale resolution and fallback: `packages/ui/src/locale.ts`.
- Four runnable adapters with the same order-desk UI: `examples/recipes/vue3`, `examples/recipes/react`, `examples/recipes/vanilla`, `examples/recipes/vue2`.

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Applies to | `@plingjs/ui` `0.1.0-alpha.2` |
| Introduced | `0.1.0-alpha.2` (first published alpha) |
| Runtime | Browsers with ES2022 modules; Node.js 20 or later for Node-side use |
| Peer dependencies | None |
| Stability | Pre-1.0 alpha; a minor release may change the API |

The theme tokens and locale catalogues on this page belong to `@plingjs/ui` at this version. Adding a catalog key is compatible; renaming or removing a public key is a breaking change for applications that use it.

# Surface protocol

Canonical: https://plingjs.dev/reference/surface-protocol

`@plingjs/surface` implements the transport-independent boundary for `pling.surface/0.1`. It projects the existing action registry into capabilities and routes an external invocation back through the application's executor. It does not authenticate callers, choose a transport, execute DOM clicks, or maintain a second permission system.

The normative semantics are in [Scope and terminology](/spec/0.1/scope-and-terminology) through [Messages and envelopes](/spec/0.1/messages-and-envelopes). This page records the exact exported API and defaults of the reference implementation.

## Public entry points

```ts
import {
  SURFACE_PROTOCOL,
  SurfaceSessionError,
  createSurface,
  type AgentSurface,
  type SurfaceOptions,
} from "@plingjs/surface";
```

| Export | Kind | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SURFACE_PROTOCOL` | constant | `"pling.surface/0.1"` |
| `createSurface(options)` | function | Creates the protocol projection |
| `AgentSurface` | interface | `describe(input?)` and `handle(request)` |
| `SurfaceSessionError` | class | Session failure from direct `describe()` calls |
| `DEFAULT_SURFACE_RECORD_LIMIT` | constant | `8` records per description by default |
| `MAX_SURFACE_RECORD_LIMIT` | constant | `100` records per description at most |

`SurfaceMethod` contains only `"describe"` and `"invoke"`. `attach`, `observe`, `handoff`, and `detach` are not part of 0.1 and must not be inferred from this package.

## `createSurface(options)`

`registry` and `execute` are required. Everything else narrows exposure, binds identity, or adds operational evidence.

| Option | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `registry` | `Registry` | required | The same registry used by the in-page agent |
| `execute` | `(id, argsJson?, context?) => Promise<ExecResult>` | required | Must call the existing executor; Surface does not reimplement confirmation, availability, or expectations |
| `app` | `string` | omitted | Application identifier copied into descriptions |
| `expose` | `readonly string[] \| (id) => boolean` | all current capabilities | Site-level allowlist; array entries may contain folded templates such as `approve@order` |
| `session` | `SurfaceSession \| () => SurfaceSession \| null` | open mode | Use a getter to re-read expiry and revocation; open mode is for local debugging only |
| `recordLimit` | `number` | `8` | Record window for `describe` |
| `maxRecordLimit` | `number` | `100` | Upper bound for a caller-supplied `limit` |
| `rateLimit` | `{ maxRequests, windowMs, limiter? }` | disabled | Applies to `handle()` and is isolated by verified session |
| `replay` | `boolean \| { windowMs?, guard? }` | disabled | Applies to `invoke`; the default guard window is five minutes when enabled |
| `onAudit` | `(event) => void \| Promise<void>` | omitted | Metadata only; no input arguments, response body, cookie, or token |
| `onAuditError` | `(error, event) => void \| Promise<void>` | omitted | Receives a failed audit write; production should attach alerting here |

### Session boundary

`SurfaceSession` contains `agentId`, `sessionId`, `userId`, `expiresAt`, an explicit `scope`, an optional `delegationId`, and an optional `revokedAt`. The transport or backend must verify all of it before constructing the session. A browser request body cannot be treated as a session.

Exposure is the intersection of `expose` and `session.scope`. Omission of `session.scope` is invalid. A session getter is evaluated for each `describe` or `handle`, so expiry and revocation take effect without restarting the page.

When a session is configured, direct `surface.describe()` throws `SurfaceSessionError`; `surface.handle()` converts the same condition into a protocol failure. Production transports should call `handle()` and return the structured response.

### Limits and replay

The built-in rate limiter is an in-process sliding window. For multiple replicas, provide a shared `SurfaceRateLimiter`. An adapter error or malformed decision fails closed with `RATE_LIMIT_UNAVAILABLE`; it must never be interpreted as permission.

Replay protection reserves `(session, request.id)` before execution. A repeated `invoke` within the window returns `REPLAY_DETECTED` and does not call the executor. The guard does not cache the earlier response. A transport-level retry therefore needs a new request id only after it has established that the previous attempt did not commit a business effect.

## `describe(input?)`

The input is optional. Accepted fields are mutually constrained:

| Field | Constraint | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `record` | one id or `1–20` ids | Return fields for those records only |
| `offset` | non-negative integer | Start of the returned record page |
| `limit` | non-negative integer | Page size; clamped to `maxRecordLimit` |
| `capabilities` | `"full"` or `"changed"` | `"changed"` may return an empty list when the capability signature is unchanged |

`record` cannot be combined with `offset` or `limit`. Unknown fields make the request invalid. The capability list can remain complete while record fields are windowed; `context.recordIds` still contains all records that can be referenced in the active regions.

The result is a `SurfaceDescription`:

```json
{
  "protocol": "pling.surface/0.1",
  "app": "orders",
  "capabilities": [],
  "context": {
    "regions": [],
    "records": [],
    "recordIds": [],
    "recordIdsTotal": 0,
    "state": {},
    "feedback": [],
    "unavailable": [],
    "recordsTotal": 0,
    "feedbackTotal": 0,
    "unavailableTotal": 0
  }
}
```

Capabilities are stable wire objects, not raw internal action views. Each capability can include `id`, `description`, `inputSchema`, `effect`, `approval`, `fidelity`, `source`, `scopePath`, `handoff`, `flowSteps`, `offscreen`, and record-template metadata.

## `handle(request)`

`handle()` accepts `unknown` and does not throw for malformed input. It returns one of three shapes:

```ts
type SurfaceResponse =
  | { ok: true; id: string; protocol: "pling.surface/0.1"; result: SurfaceDescription }
  | { ok: true; id: string; protocol: "pling.surface/0.1"; result: ExecResult; after?: SurfaceObservation }
  | { ok: false; id: string; protocol: "pling.surface/0.1"; error: { code; message; retryAfterMs? } };
```

An `invoke` request has `protocol`, `id`, `method: "invoke"`, `capability`, and an optional object-valued `input`. The id must be unique for an intended side effect and stable for retries of the same request.

A business rejection is still an `ok: true` protocol response whose `result` contains the executor's structured error. `ok: false` means the protocol could not safely reach a business result.

### Protocol failures

| Code | Typical cause |
| --- | --- |
| `INVALID_REQUEST` | Missing fields, wrong JSON shape, unknown describe fields, or invalid limits |
| `PROTOCOL_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED` | A version other than `pling.surface/0.1` |
| `METHOD_NOT_SUPPORTED` | A method other than `describe` or `invoke` |
| `CAPABILITY_NOT_EXPOSED` | The id is absent from the site allowlist or session scope |
| `RATE_LIMITED` | The session exceeded its window; inspect `retryAfterMs` |
| `RATE_LIMIT_UNAVAILABLE` | The shared limiter failed or returned an invalid decision |
| `REPLAY_DETECTED` | The same session reused an invoke id inside the replay window |
| `REPLAY_GUARD_UNAVAILABLE` | The shared replay guard failed or returned an invalid decision |
| `SESSION_REQUIRED`, `SESSION_INVALID`, `SESSION_EXPIRED`, `SESSION_REVOKED` | The verified session is missing or no longer usable |
| `INTERNAL_ERROR` | An unexpected failure outside the business result path |

## Minimal server-side composition

```ts
import { createExecutor, createPolicy } from "@plingjs/core";
import { createSurface, SURFACE_PROTOCOL } from "@plingjs/surface";

const executor = createExecutor({ registry, policy: createPolicy(confirm) });

const surface = createSurface({
  registry,
  execute: (id, args) => executor.execute(id, args),
  app: "orders",
  expose: ["orders.search", "orders.update_note@order"],
  session: () => verifiedSession,
  rateLimit: { maxRequests: 60, windowMs: 60_000 },
  replay: { windowMs: 5 * 60_000 },
  onAudit: (event) => audit.write(event),
  onAuditError: (error, event) => logger.error({ error, event }, "surface audit failed"),
});

const response = await surface.handle({
  protocol: SURFACE_PROTOCOL,
  id: "req-01",
  method: "invoke",
  capability: "orders.update_note@order",
  input: { record: "SO-1002", note: "Customer asked for a callback" },
});
```

The adapter around this call still owns authentication, HTTP, SSE, CORS, body limits, and response redaction. `surface.plingjs.dev` is a demonstration endpoint, not a shared proxy for customer applications.

## Deliberate omissions

- No generic selector click, script evaluation, raw DOM read, or arbitrary HTTP primitive.
- No browser credential parsing inside Surface.
- No business authorization replacement.
- No transport-mandated envelope framing beyond the JSON objects shown here.
- No public third-party Surface certification suite. The conformance helpers that do exist are listed in [Surface conformance and interoperability](/reference/surface-conformance-and-interoperability).

## Version and compatibility

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Applies to | `@plingjs/surface` `0.1.0-alpha.2` |
| Protocol | `pling.surface/0.1` (Draft) |
| Introduced | `0.1.0-alpha.2` (first published alpha) |
| Runtime | Browsers with ES2022 modules; Node.js 20 or later for Node-side use |
| Peer dependencies | None |
| Stability | Pre-1.0 alpha; package and protocol versions move independently |

The package version and the protocol version are separate. A `0.1.x` package release does not by itself make `pling.surface/0.1` a stable standard, and this reference does not promise compatibility with an unlisted protocol version.

# Delegation and trust boundaries

Canonical: https://plingjs.dev/reference/delegation-and-trust-boundaries

`@plingjs/delegation` is an optional browser-to-backend integration package for short-lived agent authority. It defines the credential lifecycle, reference adapters, and conformance checks. It does not own application login, tenant policy, database transactions, Redis, an audit archive, or the final business authorization decision.

Use it when an external agent must act for a signed-in user without receiving the user's Cookie or session token. If the agent runs only inside the page and uses the page's existing runtime, a delegation credential is unnecessary.

## Lifecycle

```text
authenticated user
      │
      ├─ POST /delegation/issue ──▶ plg_dlg_… token (returned once)
      │                              store keeps a SHA-256 hash
      │
      ├─ POST /delegation/introspect ──▶ public credential view
      │                                  toSurfaceSession() ──▶ SurfaceSession
      │
      ├─ POST /delegation/refresh ──▶ replacement token
      └─ POST /delegation/revoke  ──▶ revoked view
                                         │
                                         └─ event bus / SSE ──▶ page invalidates its session
```

The token is bearer authority. It must not enter a Surface response, an Agent prompt, browser telemetry, or an event payload. The safe credential view contains identifiers, scope, issue time, expiry, and revocation time only.

## Endpoints

The Web `Request → Response` handler defaults to the `/delegation` base path.

| Method and path | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /delegation/health` | Instance health |
| `GET /delegation/session` | Resolve the current authenticated user |
| `GET /delegation/events` | SSE invalidation metadata |
| `POST /delegation/issue` | Issue a credential after the user consents |
| `POST /delegation/introspect` | Validate a bearer token and return its safe view |
| `POST /delegation/refresh` | Rotate a valid credential and invalidate the old one |
| `POST /delegation/revoke` | Revoke a credential |

`createDelegationHandler({ store, events, identity, basePath?, instanceId?, now?, heartbeatMs?, maxBodyBytes? })` returns an object with `handle(request)`. The default SSE heartbeat is 15 seconds; setting it to `0` disables heartbeats. JSON request bodies default to a 32 KB limit.

`createDelegationClient({ baseUrl?, fetch?, credentials?, eventSource? })` defaults to same-origin requests at `/delegation`. Its methods are `ensureSession()`, `issue()`, `introspect()`, `refresh()`, `revoke()`, and `openEvents()`.

## Ports

### Identity

`DelegationIdentity.resolve({ request, setCookie })` returns the authenticated `{ userId, expiresAt }` or `null`. A production implementation reads its real Cookie, JWT, SSO session, or identity proxy. It must not accept a user id from the JSON body.

### Store

`DelegationStore` has four operations:

| Operation | Requirement |
| --- | --- |
| `issue` | Generate a token, persist only its hash and binding, return the token once |
| `introspect` | Validate token, user binding, expiry, rotation, and revocation |
| `refresh` | Atomically rotate; the old credential must stop working |
| `revoke` | Persist revocation and return a safe view |

The minimum binding is user, agent, session, scope, issued time, expiry, and revocation state. Scope must be deduplicated in first-seen order before persistence.

The included memory store is a local reference, not a production database. A production adapter should keep state changes and outbox rows in one transaction.

### Events

`DelegationEventBus` exposes `subscribe(userId, listener)`, `publish(event)`, and `close()`. Events are limited to:

```ts
{
  type: "credential_revoked",
  reason: "revoked" | "rotated",
  at: number,
  credentialId: string,
  delegationId: string,
  sessionId: string,
  userId: string,
  agentId: string,
  replacedBy?: string
}
```

SSE is an early-warning path, not the source of truth. Every protected action still introspects or otherwise validates the credential at the server. A lost event may delay local cleanup, but it must not preserve execution rights.

## Safe views and Surface conversion

```ts
import { createDelegationClient, toSurfaceSession } from "@plingjs/delegation";

const client = createDelegationClient({ baseUrl: "/delegation" });
const view = await client.introspect(token);
const session = toSurfaceSession(view);
```

`toSurfaceSession()` copies `agentId`, `sessionId`, `userId`, `expiresAt`, `scope`, `delegationId`, and `revokedAt` when present. It does not copy a token because the safe view does not contain one.

The resulting `SurfaceSession.scope` is still intersected with the Surface site allowlist. A delegated credential cannot expand what the application chose to expose.

## Errors and status codes

| HTTP | Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `400` | `DELEGATION_INVALID_REQUEST` | Malformed request or input |
| `401` | `DELEGATION_INVALID_CREDENTIAL` | Missing, forged, or unusable token |
| `403` | `DELEGATION_BINDING_MISMATCH` | Token does not belong to this user or session |
| `404` | `DELEGATION_NOT_FOUND` | Unknown endpoint |
| `409` | `DELEGATION_REVOKED` | Credential was revoked or rotated |
| `410` | `DELEGATION_EXPIRED` | Credential expired |
| `500` | `DELEGATION_INTERNAL_ERROR` | Backend failure with no safe detail exposed |

The browser client preserves the backend code and HTTP status in `DelegationClientError`. Do not translate `DELEGATION_EXPIRED` or `DELEGATION_REVOKED` into a prompt asking the Agent to retry. The user must reauthorize.

## Conformance checks

Before shipping a production adapter, run the reference lifecycle checks:

```ts
import {
  assertDelegationEventBusConformance,
  assertDelegationStoreConformance,
} from "@plingjs/delegation/testing";

await assertDelegationStoreConformance(productionStore, {
  userIdPrefix: `conformance-${process.env.CI_RUN_ID}`,
});
await assertDelegationEventBusConformance(productionEvents);
```

The store suite checks token redaction, scope normalization, rotation, binding, revocation, expiry, and stable error codes. Use a disposable namespace or test database. The suite creates credentials and intentionally has no cleanup API that could hide lifecycle defects.

The event-bus suite checks per-user isolation, field allowlisting, unsubscribe behavior, malformed-event filtering, and subscriber fault isolation. A process-local bus does not prove Redis, NATS, or outbox delivery; test that bridge separately.

## Boundary checklist

- The token is returned only by `issue` and `refresh`.
- The store keeps a hash, not the plaintext token.
- The user id comes only from verified identity.
- Scope is explicit and cannot exceed the Surface allowlist.
- Revocation takes effect without waiting for SSE.
- Rotation invalidates the previous token.
- Logs and metrics use credential ids, never bearer values.
- The page treats a missing lease or failed introspection as no authority.

Reference implementations cover credentials, revocation, multi-instance invalidation, package integration, production ports, and an authenticated Todo flow. They are examples, not production identity services.

## Version and compatibility

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Applies to | `@plingjs/delegation` `0.1.0-alpha.2` |
| Introduced | `0.1.0-alpha.2` (first published alpha) |
| Runtime | Browsers with ES2022 modules; Node.js 20 or later on the server |
| Peer dependencies | None; the application supplies the store, event bus, and identity adapter |
| Stability | Pre-1.0 alpha; a minor release may change the API |

Compatibility includes both this package and the implementations behind its ports. The conformance suites describe the behaviour expected at this version; they do not certify a deployment's storage, delivery, or identity provider.

# Node gateway

Canonical: https://plingjs.dev/reference/node-gateway

`@plingjs/server` is a thin OpenAI-compatible gateway. It forwards a browser request to a fixed upstream using a server-held credential, applies authentication and bounded request handling, and returns the response. It does not run the agent loop, read the page, store conversation memory, or implement tenant billing.

This separation matters: the browser still decides which declared capability to call, while the server owns provider credentials and the outbound request boundary.

## Minimal server

```ts
import { createPlingGateway, toNodeHandler } from "@plingjs/server";
import { createServer } from "node:http";

const gateway = createPlingGateway({
  upstream: {
    baseUrl: process.env.PLING_UPSTREAM_BASE_URL!,
    apiKey: process.env.PLING_UPSTREAM_API_KEY!,
  },
  model: "deepseek-chat",
  authorize: async ({ headers }) => {
    const user = await verifySession(headers.get("cookie"));
    return user ? { ok: true, user } : false;
  },
  onAudit: (event) => audit.write(event),
});

createServer(toNodeHandler(gateway)).listen(5192);
```

The browser configuration contains a same-origin path and no provider secret:

```ts
createPling({
  agent: {
    config: { baseUrl: "/api/llm/v1", model: "deepseek-chat", apiKey: "" },
  },
});
```

## Options

| Option | Type | Default | Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `upstream` | `string \| { baseUrl, apiKey?, headers? }` | required | The only target the gateway can call |
| `model` | `string` | client value | Forces the upstream model |
| `allowedModels` | `readonly string[]` | omitted | Rejects a resolved model outside the allowlist |
| `authorize` | `(ctx) => boolean \| decision` | omitted | Receives the `Request`, `Headers`, and path |
| `allowAnonymous` | `boolean` | `false` | Must be explicit for an unauthenticated local demo |
| `onAudit` | `(event) => void \| Promise<void>` | omitted | Metadata audit; callback failure is contained |
| `fetch` | `typeof fetch` | global `fetch` | Injection point for tests or a custom transport |
| `timeoutMs` | `number` | `60_000` | Waits for upstream response headers; `0` disables |
| `retry` | `false \| { maxRetries?, baseDelayMs?, maxDelayMs? }` | `maxRetries: 2` | Bounded retry before any response body is relayed |
| `maxBodyBytes` | `number` | `1_000_000` | Request body limit |

`createPlingGateway()` returns `{ handle(request: Request): Promise<Response> }`. `toNodeHandler(gateway)` adapts that interface to `node:http`; Bun, Deno, serverless handlers, and existing frameworks can call `handle()` directly.

## Routing contract

- A model request path must end with `/chat/completions`.
- `POST` is the only accepted method for model calls.
- `GET .../health` returns `{ "ok": true, "service": "pling-gateway" }`.
- The path prefix is not fixed. `/api/llm/v1/chat/completions` and `/internal/llm/v1/chat/completions` both work.
- The upstream URL is selected at construction time. A browser cannot supply a new upstream URL.

## Authentication and credentials

If neither `authorize` nor `allowAnonymous: true` is present, model calls fail closed with HTTP `503` and `GATEWAY_MISCONFIGURED`. This prevents a forgotten policy from becoming public access.

`authorize` can return:

```ts
true
// or
{ ok: true, user?: unknown, headers?: Record<string, string> }
// or
{ ok: false, status?: number, message?: string }
```

The returned `headers` are added to the upstream request. They are the explicit path for a tracing header or a short-lived provider assertion. Browser cookies are not forwarded automatically.

The provider key is read from server configuration and sent only upstream. It must never be returned in a response, audit event, browser bundle, or error message.

## Body, timeout, and retry

The body limit is enforced before parsing and before any upstream call. A request above the limit returns `413 PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE`.

The timeout covers waiting for upstream response headers, not the full streamed completion. When it expires, the gateway returns `504 UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT`.

Retry applies only while nothing has been sent to the browser. It covers:

- HTTP `408`, `425`, `429`, and `5xx`;
- network failure;
- waiting for response headers past the timeout.

It does not retry `400`, `401`, `403`, or another non-retryable status. `maxRetries` excludes the first attempt, defaults to `2`, and is capped at `5`. Delay uses bounded exponential backoff with jitter; `Retry-After` is respected but still clamped by `maxDelayMs`.

For streaming, retry stops once the response body begins to reach the browser. Replaying a partially delivered completion would duplicate content and distort usage accounting.

The browser-side agent chain also has retry logic. Keep both budgets explicit. If only one layer should retry, disable the other with `retry: false` on the gateway or a zero browser budget.

## Error shape

All gateway errors have this shape:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT",
    "message": "Upstream timed out after 3 attempts",
    "requestId": "…",
    "retryable": true,
    "attempts": 3,
    "retryExhausted": true
  }
}
```

`retryable` describes the final failure class. `retryExhausted` means this gateway has consumed its own budget; a client must not start another automatic retry loop for the same request.

| HTTP | Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `400` | `INVALID_JSON` / `INVALID_BODY` | Invalid request body |
| `400` | `MODEL_REQUIRED` / `MODEL_NOT_ALLOWED` | No model or a disallowed model |
| `401` / `403` | `UNAUTHORIZED` | Application authorization failed |
| `404` | `NOT_FOUND` | Path does not end in `/chat/completions` |
| `405` | `METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED` | Non-POST model request |
| `413` | `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE` | Body limit exceeded |
| `415` | `UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE` | Body is not JSON |
| `499` | `CLIENT_ABORTED` | Client disconnected |
| `502` | `UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE` / `UPSTREAM_ERROR` | Upstream network failure or non-2xx response |
| `503` | `GATEWAY_MISCONFIGURED` | Authentication was not configured |
| `503` | `UPSTREAM_RATE_LIMITED` | Upstream `429` after retry exhaustion |
| `504` | `UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT` | Upstream timeout |

## Audit

`GatewayAuditEvent` contains the request id, time, method, path, model, stream flag, final status, optional upstream status, attempts, duration, byte counts, optional authorized user, and final error metadata. It deliberately excludes prompts, completions, cookies, and provider keys.

Audit sink failures do not change the model response. Production should still route audit failures to its own logger or alerting system; a callback that silently disappears is not an audit trail.

## Deployment checklist

- Terminate TLS before the gateway or inside the same trusted boundary.
- Set an explicit authentication policy; never rely on a forgotten `authorize`.
- Pin the provider base URL and, where possible, the model.
- Keep request and timeout limits below the platform's own limits.
- Add a per-user rate limit in front of the gateway if the service is public.
- Send audit events to durable storage with access control and retention.
- Do not expose admin, billing, or arbitrary proxy paths from the same handler.
- Test streaming cancellation and one retry-exhaustion path before launch.

The gateway is not a policy engine, secret vault, cost-accounting service, or prompt firewall. Those controls belong in the surrounding backend and must remain independent of model compliance.

## Version and compatibility

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Applies to | `@plingjs/server` `0.1.0-alpha.2` |
| Introduced | `0.1.0-alpha.2` (first published alpha) |
| Runtime | Node.js 20 or later |
| Peer dependencies | None |
| Stability | Pre-1.0 alpha; a minor release may change the API |

The compatibility boundary is the Node.js runtime and the HTTP contract on this page. Provider-specific request and response behaviour remains the provider's contract, and this package does not depend on any UI framework.

# Vue 3 adapter

Canonical: https://plingjs.dev/reference/vue-3-adapter

`@plingjs/vue` is the reference adapter. It contains the most complete UI surface and the only implementation of the Vue-specific declaration set. It still delegates every execution decision to `@plingjs/core`, `@plingjs/dom`, and `@plingjs/agent`.

## Installation

```ts
import { createApp } from "vue";
import { createPling } from "@plingjs/vue";
import "@plingjs/vue/style.css";
import App from "./App.vue";

const pling = createPling({
  agent: {
    config: {
      baseUrl: import.meta.env.VITE_AGENT_BASE_URL,
      model: import.meta.env.VITE_AGENT_MODEL,
      apiKey: import.meta.env.VITE_AGENT_API_KEY,
    },
  },
});

createApp(App).use(pling.plugin).mount("#app");
```

Peer range: Vue 3. The adapter does not depend on Vue Router or Pinia. Router support is opt-in through `page: { router }`.

## `createPling(options)`

| Option | Default | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ui` | English, light theme | Locale, theme, message overrides, class names |
| `registry` | New registry | Reuse a registry in tests or advanced setups |
| `shared` | — | Join a `createPlingPage()` runtime; cannot be combined with `registry` / `scopes` |
| `namespace` | — | Prefix action ids for mixed-framework islands |
| `onWarn` | `console.warn` | Development warnings |
| `agent` | — | Model config, hooks, gate, trace, locale of responses |
| `diagnostics` | Vite dev only | Warn about interactive controls with no declaration; never registers actions |
| `page` | Automatic | Page identity; pass `false` to disable, or `{ router }` for Vue Router |
| `presence` | On | Action highlight; `false` disables it |
| `revealSensitive` | `true` | Render masked values in the operator's own chat view |
| `derive` | Off | Automatic derivation from native controls |
| `scopes` | Automatic | Test hooks for visibility and hit testing |

`createPling()` returns `PlingElement`: `plugin`, `registry`, `ui`, `scopes`, `page`, `feedback`, `ask()`, `inspectCoverage()`, `derived()`, and `setActiveScopes()`.

## Directives

| Directive | Value | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `v-tool` | `string` or `ToolOptions` or `ToolOptions[]` | Declare an element action |
| `v-scope` | `string` or `Scope Options` | Declare a region |
| `v-record` | `data` or a full record object | Declare a row |
| `v-task` | `string` or `{ prompt, surface?, disabled? }` | Human task entrance; never an agent action |
| `v-feedback` | String, array, or feedback object | Page feedback visible to the model |
| `v-guide-target` | `{ id, label?, description? }` | Highlight a non-action target during handoff |

```vue
<template>
  <section v-scope="{ id: 'todos', label: 'Task list', role: 'list' }">
    <li v-for="task in tasks" :key="task.id" v-record="{ data: task }">
      <button v-tool="{ id: `toggle@${task.id}`, desc: `Toggle ${task.title}` }" @click="toggle(task)">
        {{ task.done ? 'Undo' : 'Done' }}
      </button>
      {{ task.title }}
    </li>
  </section>
</template>
```

## Composables

| API | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `usePling()` | Component | Returns the installed `PlingElement` |
| `useAgentState(key, source, options?)` | Component / effect scope | Read-only view; auto-unregisters |
| `useAgentStoreState(key, store, fields \\| selector, options?)` | Component / effect scope | Pinia / Vuex field allowlist |
| `useAgentTool(options)` | Component / effect scope | Function-level action with no DOM element |

`useAgentStoreState` reads Pinia state and getters directly. For Vuex it reads `store.state` first, then `store.getters`; a missing field throws during registration.

## Components

| Component | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `<AgentDock>` | Floating or sidebar assistant; owns placement, task registration, and open state |
| `<AgentInline>` | Embed the conversation in a business column |
| `<AgentChat>` | Render the conversation without owning placement |
| `<AgentPanel>` | Development-only snapshot view; not a production assistant |

`<AgentDock>` supports `layout="dock" | "sidebar"`, `side`, `launcherPlacement`, `launcherLabel`, `quick`, `config`, `debug`, and `modelSettings`.

```vue
<AgentDock
  layout="sidebar"
  side="right"
  launcher-placement="bottom"
  :debug="{ maxCalls: 8 }"
  :model-settings="{ mode: 'byok', persist: 'session' }"
/>
```

`modelSettings` modes:

- `off` (default): no settings UI;
- `readonly`: show the application-managed connection without the key;
- `byok`: let the user enter `baseUrl`, `model`, and `apiKey`; persistence is `memory` by default, `session` optional. `localStorage` is not supported.

## Defaults that affect behavior

- No declaration means no action. `derive` is off.
- `kind` defaults to `write`; `confirm` is derived from the active approval policy.
- Action ids are generated for element bindings but should be explicit for rows.
- State values are read on every snapshot; plain objects freeze at registration.
- `inspectCoverage()` is diagnostic only. It does not make undeclared controls reachable.
- `debug` stores recent model calls in memory; it is not a privacy boundary.

## Failure modes

| Symptom | Likely cause | Check |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Action is absent from the snapshot | Disabled, covered, inactive region, or `available()` false | Open the debug inspector and read the reason |
| State remains at initial values | Plain object passed instead of a reader | Convert to `() => ({ ... })` |
| Same id appears twice | Manual id collides across rows | Include the row key or use `namespace` |
| Router changes but the model still thinks it is on the old page | `page` disabled or router not supplied | Pass `page: { router }` and whitelist query keys |
| Model settings do not appear | Mode is `off` or not passed to the mounted surface | Set `modelSettings` on `<AgentDock>` or `createPling({ agent })` |
| Debug panel shows no calls | `debug` is off, or the call was cleared | Enable `debug` and reproduce one request |

## Evidence

- Complete learning path: [Vue 3 chapters](/vue/).
- Adapter implementation: `packages/vue/src`.
- Debug inspector: `packages/vue/src/components/AgentDebug.vue`.
- Model settings: `packages/vue/src/components/AgentModelSettings.vue`.
- Runnable example: `examples/recipes/vue3`.
- Compare the [React adapter](/reference/react-adapter), [Vanilla / jQuery adapter](/reference/vanilla-jquery-adapter), and [Vue 2.7 adapter](/reference/vue-2-adapter) support tables before sharing code between adapters.

## Version and compatibility

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Applies to | `@plingjs/vue` `0.1.0-alpha.2` |
| Introduced | `0.1.0-alpha.2` (first published alpha) |
| Runtime | Vue 3 in browsers with ES2022 modules; Node.js 20 or later for SSR and builds |
| Peer dependencies | `vue ^3` |
| Stability | Pre-1.0 alpha; a minor release may change the API |

This adapter does not support Vue 2; use the separate Vue 2.7 adapter. The directives, composables, component names, and props on this page are the public surface at this version.

# React adapter

Canonical: https://plingjs.dev/reference/react-adapter

`@plingjs/react` connects React refs, effects, and context to the same page runtime used by the Vue adapters. It does not ship a second executor or a second agent loop.

Peer range: React 18 and later. The adapter is client-side; Next.js and other SSR hosts must create the instance after the DOM exists.

## Installation and provider

```tsx
import { createRoot } from "react-dom/client";
import { createPling, PlingProvider } from "@plingjs/react";
import App from "./App";

const pling = createPling({
  agent: {
    config: {
      baseUrl: import.meta.env.VITE_AGENT_BASE_URL,
      model: import.meta.env.VITE_AGENT_MODEL,
      apiKey: import.meta.env.VITE_AGENT_API_KEY,
    },
  },
});

createRoot(document.getElementById("root")!).render(
  <PlingProvider pling={pling}>
    <App />
  </PlingProvider>,
);
```

`createPling(options)` accepts `ui`, `registry`, `shared`, `namespace`, `onWarn`, `agent`, `revealSensitive`, `scopes`, `presence`, and `derive`. It returns `PlingElement` with `registry`, `scopes`, `ui`, `presence`, `derived()`, `setActiveScopes()`, and `destroy()`.

## Hooks

| Hook | Returns | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `usePling()` | `PlingElement` | Access the provider instance |
| `usePlingTool<T>(options)` | `RefCallback<T>` | Declare an element action |
| `useAgentTool(options)` | `void` | Declare a function-level action |
| `usePlingRecord<T>(value)` | `RefCallback<T>` | Declare a row record |
| `usePlingScope<T>(options)` | `RefCallback<T>` | Declare a region |
| `usePlingState(key, source, options?)` | `() => void` | Register a component-scoped read-only view |
| `exposePlingState(pling, key, source, options?)` | `() => void` | Register a view outside the component tree |

`usePlingTool` accepts the same fields as Vue's `v-tool`: `id`, `desc`, `kind`, `params`, `run`, `available`, `expect`, `confirm`, `handoff`, `action`, `target`, `autoTarget`, and `fidelity`. The options are read from a ref, so handlers do not go stale after a re-render.

## A complete row

```tsx
function TaskRow({ task, onToggle }: { task: Task; onToggle: (id: string) => void }) {
  const row = usePlingRecord({ data: task, label: task.title });
  const toggle = usePlingTool<HTMLButtonElement>({
    id: `toggle@${task.id}`,
    desc: `${task.done ? "Reopen" : "Complete"} ${task.title}`,
  });

  return (
    <li ref={row}>
      <button ref={toggle} onClick={() => onToggle(task.id)}>
        {task.done ? "Undo" : "Done"}
      </button>
      {task.title}
    </li>
  );
}
```

The ref callback registers on mount and unregisters on unmount. The record reads the latest `task` prop, so a field update does not require a second declaration.

## Region and state

```tsx
function TaskList({ tasks }: { tasks: Task[] }) {
  const scope = usePlingScope<HTMLUListElement>({
    id: "task_list",
    label: "Task list",
    role: "list",
  });

  usePlingState("task_view", () => ({
    total: tasks.length,
    open: tasks.filter((task) => !task.done).length,
  }), { description: "Task totals for the current list" });

  return <ul ref={scope}>{tasks.map((task) => <TaskRow key={task.id} task={task} onToggle={() => {}} />)}</ul>;
}
```

`usePlingState` has no setter. To change the list, declare the button or function that performs the change.

## Assistant surfaces

```tsx
<AgentDock
  title="Task assistant"
  quick={["Add a task", "Complete the first task"]}
  config={{ limits: { maxTurns: 100 } }}
/>
```

`<AgentDock>` owns the runtime, confirmation panel, handoff panel, and activity view. `<AgentChat>` is presentation-only and is useful when the host already owns the runtime and event stream.

Pass `debug` to `<AgentDock>` to enable the read-only run inspector in the activity view:

```tsx
<AgentDock debug={{ maxCalls: 8 }} />
```

The inspector shows the page projection at open time and the messages, tools, responses, and page snapshot for each retained model call. It uses the runtime that already drives the conversation; it does not execute actions or create a second session. `debug` is off by default. A number object bounds retained calls; `true` uses the default limit. Treat the inspector as a development surface: it can reveal outbound messages and page data, so do not enable it unconditionally in a public build.

Model settings remain Vue 3-only. React applications should keep credentials behind their model gateway.

## Boundaries

React supports actions, function tools, records, regions, state, confirmation, handoff, presence, derivation, namespaces, shared page runtimes, and the read-only run inspector.

It does not currently support:

- store field allowlists (`useAgentStoreState`);
- compound `steps`;
- page feedback, guide targets, or task entrances;
- model settings UI;
- coverage scanning;
- Router page identity.

Do not import Vue components to fill these gaps. Add a React implementation or move the capability into the shared layers.

## Failure modes

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hook throws because there is no provider | The component was rendered outside `<PlingProvider>` | Wrap the root |
| Action disappears after a re-render | The ref moved to a different element, or the element unmounted | Keep the ref on the stable interactive node |
| Row action targets the wrong row | id is not tied to the row | Use `toggle@${task.id}` |
| State never updates | A value was captured instead of read | Pass a function that reads current props/state |
| Dock has no model | `createPling({ agent })` and `<AgentDock>` both lack configuration | Supply `config` on one of them, or use environment variables |
| `useAgentTool` remains registered after unmount | The hook was called outside a component | Move it into the component or unregister explicitly |

## Evidence

- Adapter implementation: `packages/react/src`.
- Shared executor: `packages/core/src/executor.ts`.
- Runnable example: `examples/recipes/react`.
- Compare the [Vue 3 adapter](/reference/vue-3-adapter), [Vanilla / jQuery adapter](/reference/vanilla-jquery-adapter), and [Vue 2.7 adapter](/reference/vue-2-adapter) support tables before sharing code between adapters.

## Version and compatibility

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Applies to | `@plingjs/react` `0.1.0-alpha.2` |
| Introduced | `0.1.0-alpha.2` (first published alpha) |
| Runtime | React 18 or later in browsers with ES2022 modules; Node.js 20 or later for SSR and builds |
| Peer dependencies | `react >=18` |
| Stability | Pre-1.0 alpha; a minor release may change the API |

The adapter does not depend on Vue or on a particular router. The provider, hooks, component names, and props on this page are the public surface at this version.

# Vanilla / jQuery adapter

Canonical: https://plingjs.dev/reference/vanilla-jquery-adapter

`@plingjs/vanilla` is the DOM-level adapter. It has no framework dependency. Vue 2.7 also builds on it, which makes it the smallest executable reference for how declaration, visibility, and execution fit together.

jQuery projects use this adapter directly. There is no separate jQuery package, and none is needed: `pling.tool()` accepts any DOM element, including `$el[0]`.

## Instance

```ts
import { createPling } from "@plingjs/vanilla";

const pling = createPling({
  agent: {
    config: {
      baseUrl: "/llm/v1",
      model: "your-model",
      apiKey: "",
    },
  },
  presence: true,
  derive: false,
});

const dock = pling.dock({
  title: "Task assistant",
  quick: ["Add a task", "Complete the first task"],
});
```

`createPling(options)` accepts `ui`, `registry`, `shared`, `namespace`, `onWarn`, `agent`, `revealSensitive`, `defaultApproval`, `scopes`, `presence`, and `derive`. It returns a `VanillaPling`.

| Method | Returns | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tool(element, options)` | unbind | Declare an element action |
| `action(options)` | unbind | Declare a function-level action |
| `record(element, value)` | unbind | Declare a row record |
| `scope(element, options)` | unbind | Declare a region |
| `state(key, source, options?)` | unbind | Register a read-only view |
| `setActiveScopes(ids)` | — | Manual activation for layouts the observer cannot infer |
| `dock(options?)` | `VanillaDock` | Mount the shared assistant |
| `derived()` | controller or `null` | Access the automatic-derivation controller |
| `destroy()` | — | Stop observers and unregister declarations |

Every declaration returns an unbind function. Keep it and call it when the node is removed by code you own. The runtime also tracks the element for scope visibility; removing the node without unbinding leaves a stale registration until `destroy()`.

## Element actions

```ts
const addButton = document.querySelector<HTMLButtonElement>("#add")!;

const unbind = pling.tool(addButton, {
  id: "add_task",
  desc: "Add the text in the composer as a task",
  kind: "write",
  available: () => {
    const input = document.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>("#composer")!;
    return input.value.trim() ? true : "The composer is empty";
  },
});
```

For a fill action, declare the input itself:

```ts
pling.tool(document.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>("#composer")!, {
  id: "composer_text",
  desc: "Fill the new task text",
  action: "fill",
  params: [{ name: "text", label: "Task text" }],
});
```

For an operation with no element, use `pling.action()`:

```ts
pling.action({
  id: "clear_completed",
  desc: "Remove every completed task",
  kind: "danger",
  run: () => removeCompleted(),
});
```

## Records and regions

```ts
for (const task of tasks) {
  const row = document.querySelector(`[data-task="${task.id}"]`)!;
  pling.record(row, { data: task, label: task.title });
}

pling.scope(document.querySelector("#task-list")!, {
  id: "task_list",
  label: "Task list",
  role: "list",
});
```

Records inherit the nearest declared region. An action declared inside an inactive or covered region is removed from the model's snapshot with a reason.

## State

```ts
const offState = pling.state("task_view", () => ({
  filter,
  appliedSearch,
  matched: visibleTasks.length,
  total: tasks.length,
}), {
  description: "Current filter, applied search, and task counts",
});
```

`state` is read-only. It has no setter and does not create an action. If the model should be able to change the filter, declare the filter control with `pling.tool()`.

## jQuery shape

```js
const $ = window.jQuery;

const pling = createPling({ agent: { config: { baseUrl: "/llm/v1", model: "your-model" } } });

pling.tool($("#add")[0], { id: "add_task", desc: "Add a task", kind: "write" });
pling.scope($("#task-list")[0], { id: "task_list", label: "Task list", role: "list" });
$("#add").on("click", addTask);
```

Attach Pling after the element exists. If a plugin replaces the DOM node later, unbind the old declaration and declare the new node. Do not keep a declaration pointing at a detached clone.

## Defaults and boundaries

- `presence` is on by default; `presence: false` disables the highlight.
- `derive` is off by default.
- `kind` defaults to `write`; confirmation follows the active approval policy.
- `ui` defaults to English and the light theme.
- The adapter has no compound `steps`, page feedback, guide targets, task entrance, model settings UI, debug inspector, coverage scanner, or Router page identity.
- Surface describe/invoke is provided by `@plingjs/surface`, not by this adapter.

## Failure modes

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Action remains after the node is replaced | The old unbind was not called | Unbind before replacing the DOM |
| Action never appears | The element is detached, disabled, covered, or in an inactive region | Check `isConnected`, disabled state, and the region |
| Record fields are stale | A copy was passed instead of the live object | Pass the current business object or a reader |
| Duplicate id | A loop reused a constant id | Add the row key |
| State never updates | A snapshot value was passed | Pass a function |
| Dock has no model | No `agent.config` and no environment variables | Configure one of them |

## Evidence

- Adapter implementation: `packages/vanilla/src`.
- Runnable vanilla / jQuery example: `examples/recipes/vanilla`.
- Vue 2.7, which reuses this adapter: `examples/recipes/vue2`.

## Version and compatibility

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Applies to | `@plingjs/vanilla` `0.1.0-alpha.2` |
| Introduced | `0.1.0-alpha.2` (first published alpha) |
| Runtime | Browsers with ES2022 modules; Node.js 20 or later for builds |
| Peer dependencies | None; jQuery is optional |
| Stability | Pre-1.0 alpha; a minor release may change the API |

The adapter assumes a browser DOM and an ES2022-capable build. jQuery only affects the optional wrapper; the declaration and execution contract on this page is the same without it.
