# Vue 2 adapter

Canonical: https://plingjs.dev/reference/vue-2-adapter

`@plingjs/vue2` is a real adapter for applications that cannot move to Vue 3 yet. It installs Vue 2.7 directives and exposes a small composition API, while reusing `@plingjs/vanilla` for execution, visibility, records, state, and the assistant dock.

Supported range: Vue 2.7 only. Vue 2.6 and earlier do not provide the Composition API used by `useAgentState`; they are not supported by this adapter. They can still integrate manually through `@plingjs/vanilla`, as described below.

## Installation

```ts
import Vue from "vue";
import { createPling } from "@plingjs/vue2";

const pling = createPling({
  agent: {
    config: {
      baseUrl: "/llm/v1",
      model: "your-model",
    },
  },
});

Vue.use(pling.plugin);

new Vue({ render: (h) => h(App) }).$mount("#app");
```

The package does not prescribe a build tool. Vue 2.7 SFC projects still need their own Vue 2 compiler setup; the adapter only requires that the app runs on Vue 2.7 and that declarations are installed before components mount.

## Vue 2.6 and earlier

`@plingjs/vue2` cannot be used with Vue 2.6 or earlier. Do not install this package and attempt to register its directives in those versions. Install `@plingjs/vanilla` instead and call `pling.tool()`, `pling.scope()`, `pling.record()`, and `pling.state()` on DOM elements after the component mounts.

| Project version | Package | Declaration model |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Vue 2.7 | `@plingjs/vue2` | Directives, Composition API state helpers, and automatic lifecycle cleanup |
| Vue 2.6 and earlier | `@plingjs/vanilla` | Manual declarations and explicit unbinding |

See the Vue 2.6 section in [Install and first mount](/vue2/install-and-first-mount) for a complete example. The Vanilla path does not provide `v-tool`, `v-scope`, `v-record`, `useAgentState()`, or automatic cleanup. Records and row actions must be registered again after the list renders.

## Public API

| Export | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `createPling(options)` | Create the instance and plugin |
| `usePling()` | Read the current instance inside a component |
| `useAgentState(key, source, options?)` | Register a read-only view |
| `useAgentStoreState(key, store, fields \\| selector, options?)` | Select fields from Pinia or Vuex |
| `v-tool` | Declare an element action |
| `v-scope` | Declare a region |
| `v-record` | Declare a row record |
| `pling.dock(options?)` | Mount the shared assistant |
| `pling.action(options)` | Declare a function-level action |
| `pling.setActiveScopes(ids)` | Manual region activation |

`createPling` accepts the same options as `@plingjs/vanilla`, including `ui`, `agent`, `presence`, `derive`, `shared`, `namespace`, and `defaultApproval`.

## Directives

```vue
<template>
  <section v-scope="{ id: 'todos', label: 'Task list', role: 'list' }">
    <li v-for="task in tasks" :key="task.id" v-record="{ data: task, label: task.title }">
      <button
        v-tool="{ id: `toggle@${task.id}`, desc: `Toggle ${task.title}`, kind: 'write' }"
        @click="toggle(task)"
      >
        {{ task.done ? 'Undo' : 'Done' }}
      </button>
      {{ task.title }}
    </li>
  </section>
</template>
```

`v-tool` accepts a string, a `ToolOptions` object, or an array of options. `v-scope` accepts a region id or a full region object. `v-record` accepts row data or a full record object.

The directives register on insertion and unregister on unbind or update. Declarations inside a `v-for` should use the business key in their ids.

## Read-only state

Use the Composition API for automatic cleanup:

```ts
import { defineComponent, ref } from "vue";
import { useAgentState } from "@plingjs/vue2";

export default defineComponent({
  setup() {
    const filter = ref("all");
    const total = ref(24);

    useAgentState("task_view", () => ({
      filter: filter.value,
      total: total.value,
    }), { description: "Current task filter and total" });

    return { filter, total };
  },
});
```

Pinia and Vuex work through the same field allowlist:

```ts
const todos = useTodoStore();
useAgentStoreState("task_view", todos, ["filter", "appliedSearch", "remaining", "completed"]);
```

The field array is checked during registration. A missing field throws instead of producing an empty view. A selector can rename or compute values.

## Assistant surface

```ts
const dock = pling.dock({
  title: "Task assistant",
  quick: ["Add a task", "Complete the first task"],
});
```

The dock is the shared vanilla surface. It supports the same conversation, confirmation, handoff, activity, and telemetry behavior as the other adapters. It does not include the Vue 3 model-settings panel or debug inspector.

## Supported subset

| Capability | Status |
| --- | --- |
| `v-tool` | Supported |
| `v-scope` | Supported |
| `v-record` | Supported |
| `useAgentState` | Supported |
| `useAgentStoreState` | Supported |
| `pling.action()` | Supported |
| `pling.dock()` | Supported |
| `confirm` / `handoff` | Supported through tool options |
| `derive` | Supported through vanilla options |
| `v-feedback` | Missing |
| `v-guide-target` | Missing |
| `v-task` | Missing |
| Compound `steps` | Missing |
| Model settings UI | Missing |
| Debug inspector | Missing |
| `inspectCoverage()` | Missing |
| Router page identity | Missing |

Do not infer Vue 3 parity from the shared directive names. Compare the [Vue 3 adapter](/reference/vue-3-adapter), [React adapter](/reference/react-adapter), and [Vanilla / jQuery adapter](/reference/vanilla-jquery-adapter) support tables when moving code between adapters.

## Migration notes

- `@plingjs/vue2` requires Vue 2.7. Upgrade 2.6 when possible; otherwise use the manual Vanilla path.
- Install the plugin once, before the root component is created.
- State and tools that rely on component lifecycle should be declared in `setup()`, not in a detached helper.
- `v-feedback`, guide targets, task entrances, and compound flows require either a Vue 3 move or a new Vue 2 implementation.
- The adapter shares the vanilla dock, so styling is controlled through the shared `ui` options rather than Vue 3 component slots.

## Failure modes

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `v-tool` is ignored | Plugin was not installed before mount | `Vue.use(pling.plugin)` first |
| `usePling()` throws | Called outside a component after the root was destroyed | Keep the `createPling()` reference |
| State is never cleaned up | Declared outside `setup()` or an active scope | Declare inside `setup()` |
| Duplicate action ids | A loop reused a constant id | Include the row key |
| Record fields are stale | A copied object was passed | Pass the live row object |
| Dock has no model | No configuration and no environment variables | Configure `agent.config` |

## Evidence

- Adapter implementation: `packages/vue2`.
- Runnable example: `examples/recipes/vue2`.
- Shared execution layer: `packages/vanilla`.
- Package smoke: `pnpm pack:check` builds a separate Vue 2.7 consumer.

## Version and compatibility

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Applies to | `@plingjs/vue2` `0.1.0-alpha.2` |
| Introduced | `0.1.0-alpha.2` (first published alpha) |
| Runtime | Vue 2.7 in browsers with ES2022 modules; Node.js 20 or later for builds |
| Peer dependencies | `vue ^2.7.0` |
| Stability | Pre-1.0 alpha; a minor release may change the API |

This adapter requires Vue 2.7 and does not support Vue 3. Vue 2.6 and earlier can use `@plingjs/vanilla` manually; that is a separate integration path, not a capability of this adapter. The supported subset is the compatibility boundary; an API absent from this page is not available through this adapter at this version.

# Error codes and diagnostics

Canonical: https://plingjs.dev/reference/error-codes-and-diagnostics

Pling separates a machine-readable code from the localized sentence shown to a person. The code is stable across locales and adapters; the message comes from the shared UI catalog.

```ts
import { describePlingError, describePlingDiagnostic } from "@plingjs/ui";

const text = describePlingError(
  { code: "ACTION_UNAVAILABLE", message: "The button is covered by a dialog" },
  (key, params) => translate(locale, key, params),
);
```

Do not parse the localized text. Branch on `code`.

## Action errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical cause | What to change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `DUPLICATE_ACTION_ID` | Two actions use the same id | A loop reused a constant id | Add the row key or a namespace |
| `DUPLICATE_STATE_KEY` | Two state views use the same key | Two mounted components expose `task_view` | Give each view a unique key, or move it to one owner |
| `DUPLICATE_GUIDE_TARGET` | Two guide targets share an id | Copy-pasted handoff markup | Use unique target ids |
| `ACTION_NOT_FOUND` | The model called an id that is not registered | The declaration was removed, renamed, or never existed | Declare the action or refuse the task honestly |
| `INVALID_ARGS` | The tool-call arguments are not valid JSON or do not match the schema | The model emitted malformed arguments | Report the field and expected shape |
| `INVALID_PARAMS` | Declared parameters failed validation | Missing required value, wrong type, outside range, bad pattern | Return the validation reason; do not retry blindly |
| `PERMISSION_DENIED` | The action exists but policy rejected it | The current role may not perform it | Change the policy or the requested operation |
| `ACTION_UNAVAILABLE` | A precondition is false | Disabled control, covered element, inactive region, failed `available()` | Fix the precondition or explain it to the model |
| `EXECUTION_FAILED` | The action ran but threw | Business function rejected the operation, network failure | Surface the real reason; do not report success |
| `EXPECTATION_FAILED` | The action ran but `expect` never became true | The UI did not update, or the expectation was wrong | Check the expectation and the actual page state |
| `HANDOFF_CANCELLED` | The user declined the handoff | The operator chose not to complete the step | Stop the task, or ask for a different route |
| `HANDOFF_TIMEOUT` | The handoff exceeded its timeout | The user did not finish in time | Extend the timeout only if the business allows it |
| `HANDOFF_FAILED` | The handoff was marked done but its expectation failed | The user reported completion before the result existed | Re-check the page and ask again |
| `STEP_FAILED` | A step inside a compound action failed | One step in `steps` returned an error | Report the failing step, not the whole flow as a generic failure |
| `HOOK_BLOCKED` | A lifecycle hook blocked the action | Policy hook rejected the call | Inspect the hook result |
| `LOOP_DETECTED` | The agent repeated the same tool call too often | A missing result, wrong expectation, or a loop in the page | Fix the page or stop the run |

## Runtime errors

| Code | Meaning | Typical cause |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `NOT_CONFIGURED` | The runtime has no usable model connection | Missing base URL, model, or key |
| `LLM_FAILED` | The model request failed | Network, CORS, gateway, authentication, or provider error |
| `SEND_FAILED` | The message could not be delivered to the runtime | The session was disposed or the request was cancelled |

`NOT_CONFIGURED` is a readiness issue, not a model failure. The UI should point to the missing field instead of showing a generic request error.

## Configuration diagnostics

These codes come from `resolveAgentConfig` and are rendered through `describePlingDiagnostic`:

| Code | Missing or invalid |
| --- | --- |
| `MODEL_BASE_URL_MISSING` | OpenAI-compatible base URL |
| `MODEL_NAME_MISSING` | Model name |
| `MODEL_API_KEY_MISSING` | API key, when the endpoint requires one |
| `LIMITS_INVALID` | `maxTurns`, context budget, reserve, compaction ratio, or recent-history size |
| `RETRY_INVALID` | Retry count or delays |

A relative base URL (`/llm/v1`) is valid when the application provides a same-origin proxy. It is not a missing value.

## Limits

| Setting | Default | Valid range or interaction |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `maxTurns` | 10 | At least 1; demo fixtures may set 100 |
| `contextTokens` | 8192 | At least 1024 |
| `reserveForOutput` | 1024 | At least 0; `contextTokens - reserveForOutput` must leave at least 1024 |
| `compactRatio` | 0.8 | Greater than 0 and at most 1 |
| `keepRecent` | 6 | At least 0 |
| `maxTokens` | 1024 | Per-response output budget |
| `minActionIntervalMs` | 0 | Delay between actions in one batch |

Demo fixtures set `maxTurns: 100` explicitly. The production default remains 10.

## Reading an error correctly

1. Read `code` first.
2. Read the raw `message` only as a secondary detail.
3. Look at the current snapshot: is the action registered, available, and in an active region?
4. For `EXPECTATION_FAILED`, compare the expected result with the actual page state; do not simply retry.
5. For `ACTION_NOT_FOUND`, check whether the page changed between snapshot and call.
6. For `LLM_FAILED`, check the gateway, CORS, credentials, and provider status before changing page declarations.

## Adapter behavior

All four adapters use the same executor and the same error codes. The UI may render the message differently:

| Adapter | Error surface |
| --- | --- |
| Vue 3 | `<AgentDock>`, `<AgentInline>`, `<AgentChat>`, debug inspector |
| React | `<AgentDock>`, `<AgentChat>` |
| Vanilla / jQuery | `pling.dock()` and session events |
| Vue 2.7 | shared `pling.dock()` |

Do not map codes to adapter-specific strings in business code. Use `describePlingError` with the active UI locale.

## Related pages

- Configuration: [Install and model configuration](/vue/installation-and-model-configuration), [Connect a model gateway](/operations/connect-a-model-gateway).
- Availability and regions: [Regions, visibility, and overlays](/vue/regions-visibility-and-overlays).
- Expectations: [Actions with input and verified results](/vue/actions-with-input-and-verified-results).
- Handoff: [Confirmation and human handoff](/vue/confirmation-and-human-handoff).
- Debug inspector: [Vue 3 adapter](/reference/vue-3-adapter), `packages/vue/src/components/AgentDebug.vue`, `examples/recipes/vue3`.

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Applies to | Runtime and adapter error surfaces in `@plingjs/*` `0.1.0-alpha.2` |
| Introduced | `0.1.0-alpha.2` (first published alpha) |
| Runtime | Browsers with ES2022 modules; Node.js 20 or later for Node-side use |
| Peer dependencies | Those of the adapter being used |
| Stability | Pre-1.0 alpha; codes may be added, and an existing code's meaning is not silently changed |

The code strings and diagnostic fields on this page are the public contract for this version. A new code is an additive change; changing an existing code's category or meaning requires a documented breaking change.

# Continuity and projection

Canonical: https://plingjs.dev/reference/continuity-and-projection

Continuity answers a different question from projection. Continuity defines which page instance may continue a task and which bounded checkpoint is shared. Projection defines how controls across Shadow DOM and same-origin iframe boundaries participate in one page capability surface. Mixing them produces the wrong security model: a checkpoint is not an execution lease, and a visible iframe is not automatically shared authority.

## Continuity scopes

`@plingjs/agent` exposes three scopes:

| Scope | Storage and arbitration | Intended use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tab` | Browser `sessionStorage`, unless a custom `ContinuityStore` is supplied | MPA navigation in the same tab |
| `browser` | A same-origin browser authority; `localStorage` and lease coordination by default | Multiple tabs that may follow or explicitly take over one task |
| `remote` | A host-provided `ContinuityAuthority`, such as `@plingjs/continuity-http` | Different devices or browsers |

`scope` defaults to `tab`. `remote` requires an explicit `authority`; there is no hidden fallback to local storage.

```ts
createPling({
  continuity: {
    scope: "remote",
    authority: createHttpContinuityAuthority({ baseUrl: "/pling/continuity" }),
  },
});
```

### Checkpoint bounds

| Option | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ttlMs` | 2 hours | A checkpoint older than this is not restored |
| `maxMessages` | 20 | Maximum retained conversation messages |
| `maxEvents` | 60 | Maximum retained UI events |
| `maxChars` | 4000 | Maximum characters for one string or argument |
| `leaseTtlMs` | 30 seconds | Execution-owner lease duration |
| `takeover` | `"manual"` | Only an explicit human action may preempt an active owner |
| `maxTasks` | 20 | Shared-task discovery limit |
| `resume` | `"ask"` | User-facing resume policy |
| `returnOnDone` | disabled | Same-origin return after task completion; a delay is capped at five seconds |

The checkpoint contains a bounded task summary, recent messages, recent events, page identity, and status. It does not contain DOM, screenshots, cookies, JWTs, provider keys, or arbitrary application state.

## Authority operations

`ContinuityAuthority` is the transport-independent port:

```ts
interface ContinuityAuthority {
  list(): Promise<ContinuityTaskSummary[]>;
  read(sessionId: string): Promise<ResidencyEnvelope | null>;
  create(input: CreateTaskInput): Promise<LeaseGrant>;
  claim(input: ClaimTaskInput): Promise<LeaseGrant>;
  renew(input: RenewLeaseInput): Promise<LeaseGrant>;
  release(input: ReleaseLeaseInput): Promise<void>;
  compareAndSwap(input: CompareAndSwapInput): Promise<ResidencyEnvelope>;
  remove(input: ReleaseLeaseInput): Promise<void>;
  subscribe?(listener: (change) => void): () => void;
  dispose?(): void;
}
```

The backend must atomically check the revision and lease. A stale writer is rejected with `REVISION_CONFLICT`; it must not overwrite a newer checkpoint. `preempt: true` is reserved for an explicit user takeover. Automatic resume may join as a follower, but it must not seize an active owner.

`ContinuityChange` is notification metadata only: type, session id, revision, status, owner/lease identifiers, lease expiry, and time. It is not a second authority. A lost notification may delay a UI update, but every write still checks the current lease and revision.

## HTTP integration

`@plingjs/continuity-http` provides both sides:

- `createHttpContinuityAuthority(options)` for the browser;
- `createContinuityHandler({ backend, identity, ... })` for a Web `Request → Response` backend.

The default base path is `/pling/continuity`.

| Method and path | Operation |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /health` | Health |
| `GET /session` | Resolve identity |
| `GET /events` | SSE lease and revision metadata |
| `GET /tasks` | List the current user's tasks |
| `POST /tasks` | Create a task and lease |
| `GET /tasks/:id` | Read a checkpoint |
| `PUT /tasks/:id` | Compare-and-swap a checkpoint |
| `DELETE /tasks/:id` | Owner-only removal |
| `POST /tasks/:id/claim` | Claim or explicitly take over |
| `POST /tasks/:id/renew` | Renew the lease |
| `POST /tasks/:id/release` | Release the lease |

`userId` comes only from verified identity. It is never read from the request body. The handler maps stable backend errors to HTTP status:

| Code | HTTP |
| --- | --- |
| `UNAUTHORIZED` | `401` |
| `OWNER_MISMATCH` | `403` |
| `NOT_FOUND` | `404` |
| `TASK_EXISTS`, `REVISION_CONFLICT`, `LEASE_HELD`, `LEASE_REVOKED` | `409` |
| `LEASE_EXPIRED` | `410` |
| `INVALID_STATE` | `422` |
| `STORE_UNAVAILABLE` | `500` |

Network failure, `401`, and an unprovable lease fail closed. The page does not execute merely because it has a remembered summary.

## Projection across boundaries

### Shadow DOM

Shadow roots change the parent traversal rule, not the action model. Declarations stay on the element, and the DOM layer uses a composed tree so records, scopes, availability, and feedback can cross the boundary. There is no second registry for a shadow root.

### Same-origin iframe

An iframe is not scanned or adopted automatically. The parent explicitly calls:

```ts
import { sharePlingPageWithFrame } from "@plingjs/dom";

const stop = sharePlingPageWithFrame(frame, page);
```

The child can read or wait for that runtime:

```ts
import { plingPageFromParent, waitForPlingPageFromParent } from "@plingjs/dom";

const existing = plingPageFromParent();
const page = existing ?? await waitForPlingPageFromParent({ timeoutMs: 5000 });
```

This shared-memory path requires same-origin access. A cross-origin frame must use an explicit `postMessage` or Surface transport with its own identity and permission checks. Reading `contentWindow` failure is not an authorization result.

When embedding distinct framework islands, give each adapter a short `namespace`. IDs are prefixed with `namespace/` before appearing in actions, scopes, records, state, or feedback. Namespace collisions are visible in the full id, not hidden by separate registries.

## What not to infer

- A projected control is not automatically safe to expose. Exposure remains the `expose` and session-scope intersection.
- A checkpoint does not grant execution rights. A valid lease does.
- A visible cross-origin iframe is not a shared runtime.
- An SSE message is not durable task state.
- Browser `localStorage` coordination is not a multi-device authority.

## Verification

Run the backend conformance suite against a disposable namespace:

```ts
import { assertContinuityBackendConformance } from "@plingjs/continuity-http/testing";

await assertContinuityBackendConformance(productionBackend, {
  expiryTtlMs: 1_100,
  advanceTime: () => clock.advance(1_200),
});
```

It checks user isolation, duplicate creation, non-preempting claims, takeover, stale compare-and-swap, lease renewal, release and reclaim, owner-only removal, and expiry. The included memory backend is a testing reference, not a production store.

Relevant examples cover MPA continuity, Shadow DOM projection, same-origin iframe projection, cross-tab follow and takeover, cross-tab forks, cross-device continuity, and a server-side continuity store.

## Version and compatibility

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Applies to | `@plingjs/continuity-http` `0.1.0-alpha.2` |
| Introduced | `0.1.0-alpha.2` (first published alpha) |
| Runtime | Browsers with ES2022 modules; Node.js 20 or later for the HTTP backend |
| Peer dependencies | None |
| Stability | Pre-1.0 alpha; a minor release may change the API |

Continuity backends implement the ports in this package; the memory backend is only a test fixture. Compatibility therefore includes both the package version and the backend's conformance result.

# Surface conformance and interoperability

Canonical: https://plingjs.dev/reference/surface-conformance-and-interoperability

Interoperability means an independent client and host agree on observable protocol behavior. It does not mean both products use Pling packages, share a database, or pass an undisclosed vendor checklist.

The 0.1 repository does **not** publish a third-party Surface certification program. There is no public conformance seal, no certified vendor list, and no claim that passing the repository tests makes an implementation standards-compliant. What exists is an executable reference implementation, package-level tests, adapter conformance helpers for delegation and continuity, and reproducible examples. Those are evidence, not certification.

## Required Surface behavior

An implementation that claims `pling.surface/0.1` should demonstrate the following observable contract.

### 1. Version and method handling

- Accept the exact protocol string `pling.surface/0.1`.
- Reject another version with `PROTOCOL_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED`.
- Implement `describe` and `invoke` only.
- Reject `attach`, `observe`, `handoff`, `detach`, or an unknown method with `METHOD_NOT_SUPPORTED` unless the implemented protocol revision explicitly includes it.
- Preserve the request `id` in every response when it can be parsed.

### 2. Capability projection

- Return stable capability ids, descriptions, effect, input schema, approval requirement, fidelity, and record-template metadata when applicable.
- Keep the site allowlist and the session scope intersected.
- Never expose a capability that the executor cannot actually route.
- Treat a forbidden id as absent rather than leaking a detailed internal reason.
- Distinguish `read`, `write`, and `destructive` effects.
- Preserve developer-declared versus derived provenance when the host supports derivation.

### 3. Bounded context

- Return only the record window requested by the caller, bounded by a host maximum.
- Report totals and window metadata when records are truncated.
- Keep `recordIds` sufficient to reference an offscreen record without treating it as visible.
- Exclude raw DOM, screenshots, cookies, tokens, and unrelated store state.
- Apply the same redaction rules used by the page's assistant.

### 4. Invocation

- Validate the capability and input before side effects.
- Use the existing executor for availability, confirmation, handoff, expectations, and evidence.
- Return a business rejection as a successful protocol envelope with `result.error`.
- Do not turn a business error into a protocol error or a protocol error into a retry instruction.
- Return incremental `after` observations only when they are real and bounded.
- Never execute a capability that was absent from the session's exposure.

### 5. Session and access control

- Accept identity only from a verified transport or backend.
- Fail closed for missing, invalid, expired, revoked, or cross-user sessions.
- Reset any capability cache when session scope or expiry changes.
- Keep token parsing outside the protocol kernel.
- Make revocation effective before the next side effect, not after a notification arrives.

### 6. Limits and replay

- Apply rate limits per verified session or per open-mode bucket.
- Emit `retryAfterMs` for a rate limit when available.
- Fail closed if a shared limiter or replay guard is unavailable.
- Reserve `(session, request.id)` before an invoke side effect.
- Reject a duplicate intent without executing it again.
- Do not claim replay protection caches a response; clients must reconcile business state.

### 7. Audit

- Record identity, capability, request id, outcome, stable code, duration, and approval correlation when available.
- Exclude arguments, response bodies, credentials, and provider secrets by default.
- Route audit sink failures to an observable error path.
- Never place receipt tokens or hashes in an Agent-visible response.

## Transport interoperability

The protocol does not mandate one transport. A valid adapter may use HTTP JSON, a browser `postMessage` bridge, an in-process function call, or an MCP facade. The adapter is still responsible for:

- authenticating the caller;
- enforcing origin and CSRF rules;
- validating body size and media type;
- mapping the protocol envelope without changing error semantics;
- not inventing capabilities during tool registration;
- returning the complete protocol response, including `ok: false`;
- preserving request ids and not silently retrying a side effect.

MCP clients should see one tool per projected capability, with the schema derived from `describe`. A generic `click(selector)`, `eval`, raw fetch, or “run arbitrary JavaScript” tool is outside the protocol even if the MCP server could implement it.

## Existing automated checks

| Area | Existing check | What it proves | What it does not prove |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Surface kernel | `packages/surface/test/surface.test.ts` | Reference behavior for projection, session checks, limits, replay, audit, and envelopes | Another implementation is conformant |
| Delegation store | `assertDelegationStoreConformance()` | Token redaction, scope normalization, rotation, binding, revocation, expiry | Enterprise SSO or database transaction correctness beyond the test namespace |
| Delegation events | `assertDelegationEventBusConformance()` | Per-user isolation and allowlisted event fields | Redis/NATS/outbox delivery in a real topology |
| Continuity backend | `assertContinuityBackendConformance()` | Lease, revision, ownership, takeover, expiry, and user isolation | A browser UI correctly interprets every failure |
| MCP adapter | the local MCP reference | A concrete external tool path over the existing executor | A general certification for all MCP clients |
| Benchmark harness | the order and onboarding benchmark fixtures | Repeatable task results for two frozen fixtures | Universal token or success advantage |

The benchmark reports are intentionally narrow. The order fixture reports 60/60 passing tasks for Surface/MCP and DOM/Playwright, a median step ratio of `0.4286`, and a token ratio of `0.5085`. The onboarding fixture is a second, independent task set with mixed results; it did not reproduce the token advantage across vendors. Neither result is a cross-site or statistical guarantee.

## A practical interoperability test

Run the same small application through two independent clients:

1. Start from a signed-out state and attempt `describe`; expect a session failure, not empty success.
2. Authorize two capabilities plus one record-scoped action.
3. Confirm that `describe` exposes exactly those ids and one bounded record page.
4. Invoke a read capability twice with distinct request ids; both may succeed.
5. Invoke a write capability with a stable id, then replay the identical envelope; expect no second side effect.
6. Request a hidden capability id; expect `CAPABILITY_NOT_EXPOSED` and verify the business store is unchanged.
7. Expire or revoke the session and retry; expect a session error before the executor runs.
8. Force the audit sink to fail; verify the business response remains defined and the failure is observable in operations.
9. Close the transport during a write; reconnect and reconcile business state before deciding whether a new request id is safe.

Record the implementation version, protocol version, transport, identity adapter, fixture, and exact build. A result without those fields is not reproducible evidence.

## Claim language

Use precise claims:

- “Implements the `describe` and `invoke` methods of `pling.surface/0.1` in the reference test suite.”
- “Passed the repository's delegation-store conformance checks against a disposable namespace.”
- “Reproduced on fixture 046 with the recorded model and build.”

Avoid:

- “Certified Pling Surface.”
- “Industry-standard compliant.”
- “Secure for all agents.”
- “Works with every MCP client.”
- “Faster than browser automation” without fixture, baseline, and measured metric.

A future public conformance kit may exist, but until it is versioned, published, and independently usable, no page or implementation should imply that it does.

## Version and compatibility

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Applies to | `@plingjs/surface` `0.1.0-alpha.2` |
| Protocol | `pling.surface/0.1` (Draft) |
| Introduced | `0.1.0-alpha.2` (first published alpha) |
| Runtime | Browsers with ES2022 modules; Node.js 20 or later for Node-side use |
| Peer dependencies | None |
| Stability | Draft protocol; no public certification claim |

A passing repository fixture is evidence about that fixture, not a compatibility claim for every transport, identity provider, or MCP client. Record the package version, protocol version, transport, and fixture with every result.

# Protocol schemas and registries

Canonical: https://plingjs.dev/reference/protocol-schemas-and-registries

There are several different “schemas” around Pling. Keeping them separate prevents a familiar word from hiding incompatible contracts.

| Layer | Authority | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Capability input schema | `JsonSchema` on an action or capability | Telling an Agent what input fields are valid |
| Surface wire types | `@plingjs/surface` TypeScript types | Exact `describe` / `invoke` envelopes |
| Action registry | `@plingjs/core` `Registry` at runtime | The capabilities the current page can actually route |
| Error registries | Type unions and frozen maps in each package | Stable codes and HTTP mapping |
| Storage schemas | Application backend | Delegation, continuity, audit, and business data |

The 0.1 repository does not publish a standalone JSON Schema bundle for the Surface envelope and does not expose a public schema-registry URL. The TypeScript declarations in the packages and the normative specification are the current source of truth. A JSON Schema package should not be inferred from the presence of per-capability `inputSchema` values.

## Capability input schema

Capabilities use the `JsonSchema` type from `@plingjs/core`. It is intentionally small and oriented toward model tool declarations:

```ts
interface JsonSchema {
  type: "object";
  properties?: Record<string, unknown>;
  required?: string[];
}
```

The runtime derives this schema from declared parameters. It is not a full JSON Schema document or validator. The executor still validates values, availability, and business rules. Do not send a schema and assume that satisfying its surface shape grants permission.

### Record-scoped schemas

A folded capability such as `approve@order` omits `record` from the visible properties and exposes record-template metadata instead. The caller supplies `input.record`, and the host reconstructs the concrete executor id. A schema validator that ignores `record.total`, `record.offscreen`, or the template id can accept a structurally valid call that the host correctly rejects.

## Surface wire types

The principal exports from `@plingjs/surface` are:

| Type | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `SURFACE_PROTOCOL` | `"pling.surface/0.1"` |
| `SurfaceMethod` | `"describe" \| "invoke"` |
| `SurfaceDescribeRequest` | Describe request envelope |
| `SurfaceInvokeRequest` | Invoke request envelope |
| `SurfaceResponse` | Success or protocol failure |
| `SurfaceDescription` | Capabilities and bounded context |
| `SurfaceCapability` | One projected capability |
| `SurfaceContext` | Page, regions, records, state, feedback, unavailable items |
| `SurfaceObservation` | Bounded post-invoke change |
| `SurfaceFailure` | `ok: false` protocol error |
| `SurfaceSession` | Verified identity, expiry, scope, revocation |
| `SurfaceAuditEvent` | Metadata-only audit record |
| `SurfaceApprovalBinding` | Immutable fields an external approval backend binds |
| `SurfaceApprovalChallenge` | Human-facing challenge; token is not part of it |

JSON examples in the specification are normative for field names and meaning. TypeScript declarations add compile-time constraints but do not replace runtime validation.

## Runtime action registry

The registry is not a static protocol document. It is built by the page and changes with the current UI. A capability can disappear because:

- a region is no longer active;
- an action becomes unavailable;
- the site allowlist changes;
- the session scope changes;
- a modal or route replaces the relevant declarations.

`describe` returns a snapshot. `invoke` re-checks exposure and delegates to the executor, which re-checks availability. Caching a description forever is therefore unsafe.

## Error registries

### Surface

`SurfaceErrorCode` contains:

```text
INVALID_REQUEST
PROTOCOL_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED
METHOD_NOT_SUPPORTED
CAPABILITY_NOT_EXPOSED
RATE_LIMITED
RATE_LIMIT_UNAVAILABLE
REPLAY_DETECTED
REPLAY_GUARD_UNAVAILABLE
INTERNAL_ERROR
SESSION_REQUIRED
SESSION_INVALID
SESSION_EXPIRED
SESSION_REVOKED
```

Business execution codes are a separate `ActionErrorCode` union from `@plingjs/core`. Examples include `ACTION_NOT_FOUND`, `ACTION_UNAVAILABLE`, `INVALID_PARAMS`, `PERMISSION_DENIED`, `EXPECTATION_FAILED`, `STEP_FAILED`, and the handoff codes. They appear inside a successful Surface response because the protocol reached the executor.

### Delegation

`DELEGATION_ERRORS` is a frozen map from code to HTTP status and default message. It covers invalid request, invalid credential, binding mismatch, not found, revoked, expired, and internal error. This registry belongs to the optional delegation package, not the Surface wire contract.

### Continuity

`ContinuityAuthorityErrorCode` covers task existence, not found, revision conflict, held or expired or revoked leases, owner mismatch, unauthorized, store unavailable, and invalid state. `@plingjs/continuity-http` maps those codes to HTTP responses.

### Gateway

The server gateway returns OpenAI-compatible error bodies but uses its own stable codes, including `INVALID_JSON`, `MODEL_REQUIRED`, `MODEL_NOT_ALLOWED`, `UNAUTHORIZED`, `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE`, `UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT`, `UPSTREAM_RATE_LIMITED`, and `GATEWAY_MISCONFIGURED`. Do not reuse Surface codes for gateway failures.

## Compatibility rules

- Treat `pling.surface/0.1` as the negotiated protocol version, not the npm package version.
- Package versions use semver; protocol versions use explicit strings.
- Additive fields are allowed for tolerant readers, but a writer must not assume an older reader understands them.
- Removing a field, changing its meaning, changing an error code's category, or requiring a new method is a breaking protocol change.
- Unknown response fields should be ignored; unknown required request fields should be rejected.
- Business error codes and protocol error codes must remain separate namespaces.
- Registry state is a runtime snapshot, not a durable configuration artifact.

## Artifacts not published

The following are not published by this repository:

- a root `surface.schema.json`;
- a public schema registry service;
- generated OpenAPI or MCP server definitions for every capability;
- a machine-readable catalog of all possible business capabilities.

If these artifacts are added later, they must be generated from the same types and tested against the same fixtures. A hand-written second schema would create exactly the drift this reference is intended to prevent.

## Version and compatibility

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Applies to | `@plingjs/surface` `0.1.0-alpha.2` |
| Protocol | `pling.surface/0.1` (Draft) |
| Introduced | `0.1.0-alpha.2` (first published alpha) |
| Runtime | Browsers with ES2022 modules; Node.js 20 or later for Node-side use |
| Peer dependencies | None |
| Stability | Draft protocol; package and protocol versions are independent |

The wire types and registries are versioned with `pling.surface/0.1`; the npm package version is separate. No schema artifact is published at this version, so the types and conformance fixtures remain the reference.

# Nothing happens when the agent acts

Canonical: https://plingjs.dev/troubleshooting/nothing-happens-when-the-agent-acts

Determine three things first: did the model emit a tool call, did the call reach the executor, and did the page change. Reading only the chat text conflates three different failures.

## Decision tree

```text
No tool card in chat?
  ├─ yes: model configuration, prompt, or tool list
  └─ no: inspect the tool result
       ├─ ACTION_NOT_FOUND → id or page snapshot
       ├─ ACTION_UNAVAILABLE → preconditions / visibility
       ├─ PERMISSION_DENIED → authorization
       ├─ EXPECTATION_FAILED → executed, result not observed
       └─ success → page state or model continuation
```

## 1. Confirm the model is ready

In the debug panel, inspect `baseUrl`, model name, and configuration diagnostics. `NOT_CONFIGURED`, `MODEL_BASE_URL_MISSING`, or `MODEL_NAME_MISSING` means no valid model request was sent. Do not put a provider key in the page; production should use a same-origin model gateway.

## 2. Confirm the capability is declared and visible

Inspect the request messages and tool list:

- is the target action present?
- does the model's id match exactly?
- is it in the active region?
- does `available()` return false?
- is the control disabled or covered by a modal?

Check the stable errors in [Diagnostics and observability](/concepts/diagnostics-and-observability) and [Error codes and diagnostics](/reference/error-codes-and-diagnostics).

## 3. Separate “not executed” from “no visible change”

If the result is success but the user sees nothing:

- did the expectation wait only for a toast while the list stayed stale?
- is the record outside the current filter, page, or scroll window?
- was the store updated without a declared state view?
- is an asynchronous job still running?
- is there a cached page or duplicate component instance?

`EXPECTATION_FAILED` means the handler may have run, but the declared result did not appear. Do not resend a write immediately; read business state and check for partial success.

## 4. Check approval and handoff

A high-risk action may be `pending`. Check for an approval item, another open window, or a rejection. The agent has no approval tool. A denied confirmation should produce an explicit state, not an infinite wait.

## 5. Check transport and limits

For an external agent, check:

- the page is still connected;
- the session is valid;
- `RATE_LIMITED` was not returned;
- a `request.id` was not reused;
- the MCP facade returned the result as tool content.

`REPLAY_DETECTED` means no business action ran. Do not mint a new id for the same intent to bypass it; query the prior result first.

## Minimal reproduction

Capture the user request, tool id, arguments, execution result, page snapshot, and timestamp. Replay with a deterministic scripted model. If replay works, the issue is model selection; if not, inspect declaration, availability, or transport.

## Verify the fix

- Manual click and agent invocation produce the same business result.
- The success condition observes a real change.
- Unavailable actions explain why.
- Repeated calls do not write twice.
- Theme and locale do not change action ids.

---

# Action not found

Canonical: https://plingjs.dev/troubleshooting/action-not-found

`ACTION_NOT_FOUND` means the executor's current page registry has no such id. It is usually a declaration, snapshot, or naming problem, not a model capability problem.

## Common causes

| Cause | Symptom | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dynamic id mismatch | Row key or delimiter differs | Generate ids through one function and test it |
| Action in an unmounted region | Call after a modal closes | Remove registration on close; describe before calling |
| Page navigated | Old snapshot id is absent from the new page | Describe after navigation |
| Namespace collision | Two components share a prefix | Use a unique scope or namespace |
| Stale build | Old bundle lacks the new action | Clear cache and verify the build version |
| Expired snapshot | Record or region changed after observation | Bound snapshot lifetime and refresh on change |

## Diagnostic order

1. Copy the id from the current debug snapshot, not chat history.
2. Check whether the action appears in the tool list; if not, inspect declaration and conditional rendering.
3. For a folded action, confirm the target record is still referenceable.
4. Check route and modal state.
5. If namespaces are enabled, check that the caller includes the prefix.
6. Run the same action through the in-page assistant; failure there points to page declaration.

## Dynamic ids

```ts
const toggleId = (taskId: string) => `toggle@${taskId}`;
```

Do not write `` `toggle-${id}` `` in one place and `` `toggle@${id}` `` in another. The id is a protocol contract, not display text.

If an id depends on list position (`row-1`), sorting or filtering points it at another record. Use a stable business key.

## Snapshots and navigation

An action existing once does not mean it exists forever. After navigation, the old registry may be destroyed and the new page may not be mounted. An external client must `describe` again when page identity changes. Do not reuse old capabilities across SPA, MPA, iframe, or Shadow DOM boundaries. See [Continuity and projection reference](/reference/continuity-and-projection).

## Prevent recurrence

- Generate each family of ids through one function.
- Assert the id-to-record relationship in tests.
- After navigation or modal close, assert old ids are unavailable.
- Inspect the tool list after a build.
- Do not describe “not found” as permission denial; recovery differs.

## Related

[The page capability model](/concepts/the-page-capability-model), [Error codes and diagnostics](/reference/error-codes-and-diagnostics).

---

# Action is unavailable

Canonical: https://plingjs.dev/troubleshooting/action-is-unavailable

`ACTION_UNAVAILABLE` means the action is registered but cannot execute now. This differs from a missing action: the declaration exists, but a business or interface gate rejects it. Explain and clear the precondition; do not retry or seek a bypass.

## What to inspect

| Check | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `available()` | Whether a business precondition returns false |
| `disabled` | Whether the native control is disabled |
| Region | Is the action in an active region, modal, or hidden step? |
| Overlay | Is a modal, loading mask, or fixed layer covering the target? |
| Record state | Is the row locked, deleted, or owned by another user? |
| Role | Does the current user have permission? |
| Filter / page | Has the target left the current business view? |

## Read the reason

The message may name a precondition, record state, or active region. It gives direction, but program logic still uses the stable code. The debug panel should retain action id, target record, and the snapshot at failure time.

The executor returns a structured result rather than throwing:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "ACTION_UNAVAILABLE",
    "message": "Action is currently unavailable: approve@order:SO-1042; reason: order is locked"
  }
}
```

The example reason is page-defined. Do not parse the message for control flow; expose a stable business reason in your own diagnostics if operators need to group failures.

## Diagnostic sequence

1. Copy the action id and target record from the failed request, not from an older transcript.
2. Describe the page again. Confirm that the action is still present and that its region is active.
3. Compare the present DOM with the page snapshot: disabled control, hidden step, closed dialog, or replaced row.
4. Call the page's read path or state view to establish the current business record.
5. If the control is outside the viewport, use a declared reveal or scroll capability before retrying.
6. If a person must unlock, approve, or complete a prerequisite, stop and hand off the task.

Do not “repair” the situation by switching to a similar action, issuing DOM clicks, or editing the record directly. Those paths bypass the contract that made the action safe in the first place.

## Do not

- retry an unavailable action unchanged;
- switch to a similar id to bypass permission;
- use generic clicking or scripts to fake availability;
- treat “waiting for approval” as unavailable;
- change business state without human authorization.

## Recovery

1. A missing prerequisite: perform an allowed prerequisite, then describe again.
2. A filtered target: restore the filter or choose a new business view.
3. A covered control: close or complete the modal.
4. A locked record: ask its owner to resolve it.
5. Insufficient permission: hand off to a person; the agent cannot self-authorize.
6. A `handoff`: show the human action and wait for the result.

## Page design

- Return a specific reason instead of a bare false.
- Keep ids stable; do not make an action disappear when it is merely unavailable unless the business must conceal it.
- Distinguish confirmation, handoff, and unavailability.
- Expose step, role, and record state that affect availability.

## Acceptance

- An unavailable action never runs its business handler.
- The returned message names a concrete precondition when one exists.
- Re-describing after the prerequisite is cleared makes the action available again.
- Permission failures remain distinct from temporary interface state.
- A retry after restoration does not duplicate the earlier business effect.

## Related

[Execution lifecycle](/concepts/execution-lifecycle), [Approval and human handoff](/concepts/approval-and-human-handoff), [Error codes and diagnostics](/reference/error-codes-and-diagnostics).

# Confirmation denied or stuck

Canonical: https://plingjs.dev/troubleshooting/confirmation-denied-or-stuck

When approval breaks, an agent often says “still waiting,” “the action did not complete,” or polls repeatedly. First establish whether the request is genuinely pending, rather than conflating network timeout, unmounted UI, and business rejection.

## Identify the state

| Observation | Meaning | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No approval UI | Request not created, or UI not mounted | Check host and region |
| UI exists but user cannot see it | Hidden window, overlay, or another tab | Provide a discoverable pending-action entry |
| User rejected | Explicit business decision | Return rejection and stop the intent |
| User approved but no result | Receipt not consumed, execution failed, or expectation failed | Check backend and result |
| Agent polls forever | No terminal state or polling bound | Return structured pending / failed / timeout |

## Common failures

**Treating `approval: ask` as auto-approval.** It declares a requirement. The agent has no approval action and must not see an approval token.

**The pending item is bound to the wrong request.** A challenge must bind request id, capability, record, argument digest, user, agent, and session. Otherwise the human sees one action and another executes.

**Approval remains after the page unloads.** Cancel or transfer the request and return a diagnosable state. Do not leave the agent polling forever.

**Approval is recorded only in the frontend.** A high-risk action should be verified by a backend with a one-time receipt before the business transaction.

**Timeout is treated as rejection.** Their meanings differ. A timeout means unconfirmed or unknown; do not auto-retry a write.

## Recovery

1. Query approval and execution state by request id.
2. If still pending, show a clear summary and expiry.
3. If rejected, stop; do not try a similar action to bypass.
4. If a receipt was consumed but business failed, read business state and check for partial success.
5. After refresh, describe again; do not reuse the old request.

## Acceptance

- Rejection, timeout, page close, and receipt reuse have stable errors.
- The business handler did not run before approval.
- The agent sees no approval secret and has no approval capability.
- Audit links to a public approval id.
- Polling is bounded and obeys rate limits.

## Related

[Approval and human handoff](/concepts/approval-and-human-handoff), [Approval, audit, and revocation for agent actions](/recipes/approval-audit-and-revocation-for-agent-actions).

# Model request fails

Canonical: https://plingjs.dev/troubleshooting/model-request-fails

A model request failure is not a page action failure. It may come from missing configuration, a wrong base URL, authentication rejection, CORS, gateway timeout, or provider rate limiting. Establish where the request went before inspecting the response.

## Quick diagnosis

| Symptom | Likely cause |
| --- | --- |
| `NOT_CONFIGURED` | Incomplete model configuration |
| Network error / CORS | Browser calls a cross-origin endpoint directly, or same-origin routing is missing |
| `401` / `403` | Gateway authentication or upstream credential failure |
| `429` | Provider limit or exhausted gateway retries |
| `502` / `504` | Upstream unavailable or timed out |
| Streaming interruption | Proxy buffering, connection timeout, cancellation |
| No response and no error | Request not mounted, session destroyed, UI not rendered |

## Configuration checks

Confirm:

- production uses a same-origin relative path such as `/api/llm/v1`;
- the model is a fixed alias allowed by the gateway;
- the browser holds no provider key;
- the gateway has `authorize` rather than anonymous access;
- the upstream URL comes only from the server;
- timeout and retry budgets do not multiply across layers.

Show `MODEL_BASE_URL_MISSING`, `MODEL_NAME_MISSING`, `MODEL_API_KEY_MISSING`, and `LIMITS_INVALID` as configuration diagnostics, not one vague model failure.

## Gateway checks

Use the request id to inspect:

- returned and upstream status;
- attempts, retryability, and exhaustion;
- model allowlist;
- body size and timeout;
- whether prompts or credentials entered logs.

Do not leave authentication disabled after debugging, and do not return raw upstream errors to the browser.

## Client handling

- 401/403: reauthenticate or fix configuration; do not retry automatically.
- 408/429/5xx: honor retryability and backoff.
- Failure after streaming starts: do not replay the whole request; present a recoverable state.
- `retryExhausted`: do not add another retry loop in the browser.
- Page action succeeded but model failed: retain the tool result and continue from current state after reconnect.

## Security boundary

Model keys live only on the server. `VITE_*` or equivalent frontend variables enter the build and are not secret storage. Logs must not contain Authorization, full prompts, or response bodies unless the application explicitly chooses and is permitted to retain them.

## Related

[Connect a model gateway](/operations/connect-a-model-gateway), [Model access and trust boundaries](/concepts/model-access-and-trust-boundaries), [Error codes and diagnostics](/reference/error-codes-and-diagnostics).

# Records stale or duplicated

Canonical: https://plingjs.dev/troubleshooting/records-stale-or-duplicated

A record view is a business projection at one moment. It can become stale or duplicated through async updates, pagination, filtering, unstable ids, or double-mounted components. Do not patch by position or display text; fix ids and snapshot lifetime.

## Common causes

| Cause | Symptom |
| --- | --- |
| Unstable record id | Sorting makes an action target the wrong row |
| Array index used as key | Deletion reuses old component state |
| Double mount | A record appears twice or an action executes twice |
| Async race | An old response overwrites newer records |
| Stale snapshot | Agent uses a deleted or updated record |
| Pagination / virtual list | Agent sees a window but assumes the whole set |
| Multiple tabs | Two pages maintain different state |

## Principles

1. Derive record ids from business keys, not array positions.
2. Recheck the target record before execution; the protocol validates folded record ids.
3. Refresh descriptions after navigation, filtering, sorting, pagination, or writes.
4. Give each record one projection owner to avoid duplicate registration.
5. Expose totals and windows explicitly; never truncate silently.
6. Version or cancel async responses so an old response cannot overwrite a newer state.

## Duplicate execution

If one user action creates two records:

- check for a double-mounted frontend component;
- check whether the model called twice;
- check whether the transport retried an executed request;
- check backend idempotency constraints;
- check whether `request.id` was reused or wrongly treated as a business idempotency key.

Replay protection prevents reuse of one request id in a session; it does not make the business handler idempotent. Production writes still need database constraints or idempotency tokens.

## Diagnostic steps

1. Capture before/after snapshots and `changed.records`.
2. Compare record ids, counts, and update times.
3. Look for two page instances or two agents operating concurrently.
4. Use a read action to confirm backend truth.
5. If page and backend disagree, fix synchronization before permitting writes.

## Acceptance

- Sorting, filtering, and deletion keep ids bound to the same business object.
- Old records are not callable after navigation.
- Pagination exposes total and next position.
- Retry does not write twice.
- Multi-tab conflicts have an explicit policy.

## Related

[Records, row actions, and change evidence](/vue/records-row-actions-and-change-evidence), [Long lists, scrolling, and offscreen actions](/vue/long-lists-scrolling-and-offscreen-actions), [Context model](/spec/0.1/context-model).

# Navigation loses the task

Canonical: https://plingjs.dev/troubleshooting/navigation-loses-the-task

A full-page navigation destroys the old document's runtime, registry, and element references. An SPA route usually replaces only components, so the two need different fixes.

## Identify the navigation type

| Type | Symptom | Key issue |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SPA route | No page reload, but tools or regions disappear | Component unmount, route guard, keep-alive |
| MPA navigation | History and pending requests vanish | Continuity checkpoint |
| Iframe navigation | Parent persists, child runtime rebuilds | Explicit sharing and scope |
| Multiple tabs | Task continues elsewhere | Owner lease and explicit takeover |

## SPA

1. Check whether the action lived in an unmounted component.
2. Check whether the page describes again after route change.
3. Check whether keep-alive left an old registration.
4. Check for unique ids or namespaces per route.
5. Check whether an expectation waited across navigation and became invalid.

After navigation, obtain page identity and capabilities again. Do not carry old-route actions into a new route.

## MPA

MPA does not retain element references and cannot restore “approved” state. A continuity checkpoint contains only task goal, summary, recent events, and page identity. It must not contain Cookies, tokens, approval, or raw sensitive values.

Recovery policies:

- `ask`: show a “continue previous task” entry;
- `auto`: send a controlled continuation after the page is ready;
- `off`: restore history without starting.

In every policy, the current page must redeclare capabilities. An action from the previous page does not regain authority.

## Interrupted execution

If a full navigation happens during a tool call, the result may be unknown. History should contain a synthetic result saying the page navigated during execution and the business result is unconfirmed. Read business state before retrying a write.

## Cross-tab

Cross-tab tasks need a lease: one owner executes at a time. A follower may observe but not silently take over. Takeover or fork is a user action. A shared string in storage is not ownership.

## Acceptance

1. Old capabilities cannot be invoked after navigation.
2. New capabilities appear after a fresh description.
3. Checkpoints contain no credentials, approval, or full sensitive values.
4. Recovery does not resubmit an interrupted write.
5. Owner loss, lease expiry, and task completion have distinct UI states.
6. Multiple tabs cannot write the same task concurrently.

## Related

[Task continuity across pages and tabs](/concepts/task-continuity-across-pages-and-tabs), [MPA and task continuity](/vanilla/mpa-and-task-continuity), [Continuity and projection reference](/reference/continuity-and-projection).

# Sensitive value leaks or is missing

Canonical: https://plingjs.dev/troubleshooting/sensitive-value-leaks-or-is-missing

Sensitive-value bugs have opposite forms: the model sees raw text it should not, or an action needs a value and receives a mask. First establish the intended exposure mode, then inspect execution-time restoration and outbound redaction.

## Modes

| Mode | Model sees | Action receives | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `hidden` | `[hidden]` | Nothing usable | Indicate existence only |
| `masked` | Lossy mask | Not reversible | Human tail check |
| `token` | Short-lived alias | Real value at execution | Action truly needs it |
| `hint` | Type description | Nothing usable | Explain the field |

The default is `hidden`. If an action needs a real phone number, use a token and protect the action; do not pass a mask to business code.

## Leak investigation

1. Check that records, state, feedback, and errors all apply the same sensitivity declaration.
2. Check whether business code interpolates a real value into `message`; outbound redaction is a safety net, not the only defense.
3. Check application logs, APM, analytics, and URL parameters. Leakage outside the framework boundary is not automatically fixed.
4. Check tool results, debug panels, and audit events for raw arguments.
5. Check whether tokens enter localStorage, cross-session URLs, or third-party services.
6. Check whether `sensitive()` is nested in a way that prevents detection.

## Missing-value investigation

1. Confirm the field uses token, not masked/hidden.
2. Confirm the token belongs to the current page session; old aliases may expire after refresh.
3. Confirm arguments remain an object and the schema does not reject an alias format.
4. Confirm business code receives executor-restored arguments.
5. Confirm error redaction is not so broad that diagnosis is impossible; use record id or field name.

Unknown or forged tokens MUST be rejected before execution. Business code must not parse `{p:...}` itself; that is executor responsibility.

## Audit and debug

A debug panel may show an alias or mask, never the real value. Audit keeps record id, capability, outcome, and public approval id, not full arguments.

## Acceptance

- One field follows the same rule in records, state, feedback, and errors.
- A mask cannot be used for a write.
- Tokens are valid only in the current page session.
- A forged token is rejected and the business handler does not run.
- Application logs and analytics do not collect raw values.
- Debug, audit, and model context do not expose original values.

## Related

[Sensitive data](/vue/sensitive-data), [Context and sensitive data](/surface/context-and-sensitive-data), [Security and privacy specification](/spec/0.1/security-and-privacy).

# Too many tokens or steps

Canonical: https://plingjs.dev/troubleshooting/too-many-tokens-or-steps

An expensive run usually comes from unbounded context, oversized record windows, broad tool results, undetected loops, or a turn budget that hides a page problem. It is rarely just “a weak model.”

## Measure first

Record:

- `turnsUsed`: model round trips in this request;
- `telemetry.summary().llmCalls`: cumulative session calls;
- estimated tokens and tool-result size per request;
- the actual tool sequence;
- compaction count;
- failures and retries.

Do not mix cumulative calls and per-request budget. Find whether growth comes from history, tool output, or repetition.

## Common causes

| Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| Oversized record window | Reduce `limit`; read individual records on demand |
| Repeating the full page description | Use `capabilities: "changed"` and `after` |
| Exposing the whole store | Expose only task-relevant fields |
| Tool returns large HTML/JSON | Return a business summary and changed ids |
| Model repeats the same action | Inspect expectations, errors, and loop detection |
| Unbounded history | Configure `contextTokens`, `compactRatio`, `keepRecent` |
| Excessive turn budget | Start from production default 10 and measure before raising |

## Suggested configuration

```ts
limits: {
  maxTurns: 10,
  contextTokens: 8_192,
  reserveForOutput: 1_024,
  compactRatio: 0.8,
  keepRecent: 6,
  maxTokens: 1_024,
}
```

`maxTurns` bounds one `send()`, `contextTokens` bounds prompt history, and `maxTokens` bounds one generation. They are different controls. Raising `maxTurns` from 10 to 100 does not compact history; it only gives a loop more chances.

## Design smaller context

- expose only fields needed for the current decision;
- return a window, total, and referenceable ids for long lists;
- use `after` instead of describing the entire page after success;
- convert large files into a business summary or job id;
- keep stable instructions in capability descriptions rather than repeating them in every user turn;
- stop on a definite failure instead of treating it as a new prompt.

## Loop detection

If the model repeats the same id and arguments:

1. check whether the tool result indicates success;
2. check whether the expectation can ever become true;
3. check whether the page rebuilds on every call;
4. check whether the error gives actionable information;
5. verify `LOOP_DETECTED` and the turn limit.

Do not solve a loop by raising the budget. It turns a bug into a larger bill.

## Acceptance

- A 100-record page has predictable token use under the default window.
- A successful action does not trigger a full page description.
- Repeated failure terminates with a structured error.
- The task still completes after compaction.
- Token and step growth can be explained by request id.

## Related

[Runtime limits, observability, and error codes](/vue/runtime-limits-observability-and-error-codes), [Agent runtime, sessions, context, and limits](/reference/agent-runtime-sessions-context-limits), [Testing, coverage, and evaluation](/vue/testing-coverage-and-evaluation).

# SSR or hydration breaks the page

Canonical: https://plingjs.dev/troubleshooting/ssr-or-hydration-breaks-the-page

The server has no `window`, `document`, `MutationObserver`, or real event loop. Browser-only initialization at module top level fails during SSR; placing it in first render can also cause hydration mismatch.

## Symptoms

| Symptom | Likely cause |
| --- | --- |
| `window is not defined` | Browser code runs during module import |
| Hydration mismatch | Server and client render different initial DOM |
| Actions unavailable on first paint | Plugin installs after mount |
| Double registration | Server render and client initialize twice |
| Crash after route change | Singleton reused across requests |
| Leaked listeners | Plugin teardown does not clean up |

## Vue / Nuxt

- create `createPling()` inside a plugin or after `onMounted`;
- do not share a module singleton across requests;
- use a `.client` plugin or an explicit client condition;
- keep server and client initial markup identical before hydration;
- recreate page declarations on route change, or ensure scope cleanup is correct.

See [Nuxt and SSR](/vue/nuxt-and-ssr).

## React / Next.js

- use the provider in a client component and check the `"use client"` boundary;
- never touch browser globals at module top level;
- avoid rendering different DOM on the first render based on `window`;
- create the runtime in an effect or after client mount;
- do not pass non-serializable instances or functions from server components.

See [Next.js and SSR](/react/next-js-and-ssr).

## Diagnostic order

1. Find the first `window` / `document` access in server logs.
2. Inspect hydration warnings and component boundaries in the browser.
3. Disable Pling initialization and confirm base SSR works.
4. Move runtime creation into a client lifecycle.
5. Check duplicate plugin installation and singleton reuse across requests.
6. Test a real production build, not only a dev server.

## Security and consistency

An SSR page can return signed-out or placeholder markup first. Do not write protected data into server HTML and then let the client surface assume login. Revalidate identity per request; do not cache request sessions in a global module.

## Acceptance

- Server rendering accesses no browser API.
- Hydration emits no structural mismatch warning.
- Actions appear at a documented point after first paint.
- Two concurrent requests do not share user state.
- Route changes and unmount clean up listeners and registrations.
- SSR and client behavior are tested in a production build.

## Related

[Nuxt and SSR](/vue/nuxt-and-ssr), [Next.js and SSR](/react/next-js-and-ssr), [Projection: Shadow DOM and iframes](/concepts/projection-shadow-dom-and-iframes).

# Start here

Canonical: https://plingjs.dev/start/

Pling is a capability layer for web applications. It gives an agent a defined set of operations that your application already knows how to perform. The agent does not scan the page and guess which button to press; it chooses from actions your team has declared.

Pling does not replace Vue, React, the DOM, or your backend. It adds a contract between the page and the agent, and a runtime that executes declared actions through the page's existing behaviour.

## Start with a framework

**Vue 3** — [Quick start: add Pling to a Vue app](/vue/quick-start-add-pling-to-a-vue-app)  
Add the plugin, declare the controls for one task, and mount an assistant on a working Todo page.

**React** — [Quick start: add Pling to a React app](/react/quick-start-add-pling-to-a-react-app)  
Install the provider, declare one action, and mount the assistant in your React application.

If you want to see the interaction before installing anything, open the [live examples](/examples/).

## What you need

Both quick starts assume:

- a Vue 3 or React application;
- Node.js 20 or newer for the tutorial tooling;
- a model endpoint that accepts requests in the OpenAI-compatible chat format.

During local development, the page may call the model endpoint directly. In production, model traffic should pass through your own server or gateway so that credentials and policy remain outside the browser.

Pling does not include a hosted model or a fixed model provider. The application decides which endpoint to use and how requests are authenticated.
